stories.title: Yogi announces 1 lakh new police jobs:Openings for home guards, sub inspectors; 936 radio operators get joining letters
stories.summary: CM Yogi announced on Tuesday in Lucknow that 1 lakh new recruitments will be made in UP Police this year. He said - recruitment will be done for Home Guard, Police, and Sub-Inspector posts. The CM distributed joining letters to 936 radio operators. He also took photos with them. The CM said - in the last 9 years, more than 2 lakh 20 thousand policemen have been recruited in a fair manner, which is a record in itself. More than 500 skilled players have been included in the police force. As a result, the state is performing better in national and international competitions. Chief Minister Yogi’s key statements 1. “No need for recommendations for jobs now” The Chief Minister said that just two days ago, 60,000 constables passed out together at 112 centres. This means 60,000 new personnel have joined the UP Police and will now serve actively in the field. He said they have become part of not only the country’s but the world’s largest civil police force, and will serve a population of 25 crore through its communication network. He added that throughout the recruitment process, no candidate needed any recommendation or money. The entire process was completed in a fair and transparent manner, based only on merit, ability and reservation rules. The result is now visible to everyone. 2.“Our aim is to give opportunity to every deserving youth” Yogi said their only goal is to provide opportunities to every capable and deserving young person who wants to join the Uttar Pradesh Police. He said before 2017, there were 10 districts without police lines, and many police stations did not even have proper buildings or basic facilities like barracks. He added that today, old barracks have been replaced with high-rise buildings. Model police stations are being built, new fire stations are being set up, and forces like SSF and SDRF have been formed. Three new women police battalions have also been created. Although three new laws came into force in July 2024, Uttar Pradesh had already prepared for them in advance. The Chief Minister said the State Forensic Institute is now functioning successfully. Keeping the importance of forensic evidence in mind, two mobile forensic labs are working in every district with trained staff, technicians and sample collection teams. 3. “Rule of law is the first guarantee of development” Yogi said this is the story of a new Uttar Pradesh, where the police are not only ensuring a crime-free and riot-free environment but are also contributing to India’s economic growth. He said the police play an indirect but major role because rule of law is the first condition for development. He added that a strong law-and-order system is attracting investors from India and abroad, making it easier to build modern infrastructure. He said when there is strong intent, results naturally follow. The Chief Minister also stressed that every police personnel must remain physically fit, as physical fitness leads to mental strength. Only then can they serve the nation with honesty and dedication. He said communication is a key part of any system, and better communication makes police and security forces stronger and more effective. 4. “There was discrimination in jobs earlier” The Chief Minister said some candidates shared their success stories from the recruitment process, showing they wanted a fair and honest selection. He said the process has been completed transparently, and now it is the responsibility of recruits to perform their duties with the same integrity. He added that India can only progress when every citizen works honestly in their field. No caste, religion or personal interest can be above the nation. He said this was not possible nine years ago. Earlier, recruitment processes were not completed properly, there were allegations of bribery, and discrimination was common. Today, if a person has ability, nothing can stop them from moving forward. This kind of environment has now been created in the state.

stories.title: KGMU doctor sacked over molestation charge:Woman alleges bad touch during ultrasound; attendant removed
stories.summary: A doctor accused of molesting a female patient during an ultrasound at the Urology department of King George’s Medical University (KGMU) has been dismissed from his job. The accused AYUSH (Ayurveda, Yoga Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy) doctor had been hired by a private agency to operate the ultrasound machine under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model. Initially, officials tried to suppress the matter after the woman filed a complaint. However, following public criticism, the administration set up an inquiry committee. The investigation found the patient’s allegations to be true. After this, both the doctor appointed by the agency and the ward attendant working on an outsourcing basis were removed from their jobs. Officials suppressed the matter for several days A woman residing in Kakori experienced urological problems. On April 1, the female patient arrived at KGMU for treatment. A doctor from the Urology department examined the patient. They advised her to undergo an ultrasound and other tests. The woman went to the Urology department for the ultrasound examination. The victim accused Dr. Shoaib, an AYUSH doctor deployed through an agency, of molestation during the ultrasound. She filed a written complaint with the Head of the Department. For a long time, officials suppressed the matter. The victim continued to lodge complaints. Following this, the KGMU administration formed a 7-member inquiry committee. 7-Member Inquiry Team Submitted Report in 14 Days A team of 7 senior doctors, including Prof. Apul Goyal, Head of the Urology Department, investigated the complaint. During this, it was confirmed that there was no other female staff present at the time of the ultrasound, apart from the doctor. After two weeks of investigation, the team submitted the report to the Vice-Chancellor. Meanwhile, instructions for action were issued from the Vice-Chancellor's office. Under these instructions, the services of the accused and ward staff Savita were terminated. Doctor-Attendant Removed Spokesperson Dr. K.K. Singh stated - Based on the investigation committee's report, the Ayush doctor deployed through an agency has been removed from KGMU. A ward attendant should be present with the female patient during the ultrasound. Negligence was also shown in this. Therefore, the ward attendant on duty has also been removed from service. The PPP Model Game in the Urology Department KGMU has a Radiology department. Approximately 12 regular doctors are deployed in the department. There are more than 40 resident doctors. The department operates ultrasound, CT scan, MRI, X-ray, and other machines. The department is continuously enhancing quality facilities for radiodiagnosis tests. Despite this, the game of operating machines on a PPP model is going on in KGMU. Companies are making huge profits in KGMU. In return, KGMU is receiving a meager commission. In the Urology department too, ultrasound machines have been operated on a PPP model for about 20 years. Who is conducting the tests in these? KGMU administration is not concerned about this.

stories.title: UP voters want renomination of 39 MLAs on caste basis:Thakur, Brahmin lawmakers are top choice
stories.summary: Caste continues to play a decisive role in Uttar Pradesh politics. According to Dainik Bhaskar’s extensive survey, 39 MLAs were preferred by over 50% of respondents for renomination primarily based on caste. Among them, the highest number 11 MLAs belong to the Thakur community, followed by 6 Brahmin MLAs. In third place are Yadav and Kurmi legislators, with 4 MLAs each. The remaining 14 MLAs belong to other caste groups. However, MLAs from Lodhi, Gurjar, and Rajbhar communities were largely rejected by respondents for renomination. Samajwadi Party faces highest rejection among MLAs The survey reveals that 95 MLAs from the Samajwadi Party (SP) were disliked by voters. Among them, 20 are from the Yadav community. Interestingly, even among the 8 SP MLAs who were liked, 4 belonged to the Yadav caste. Majority of MLAs face public disapproval A significant 361 out of 400 MLAs were not preferred for renomination. Among these: Party-wise caste-based rejection trends Caste a key factor in voter perception In 396 out of 400 cases, respondents cited caste as one of the factors influencing their opinion about MLAs. However, caste alone was not the sole reason for rejection. Only 8 MLAs saw caste emerge as a relatively stronger factor in public opinion. Mixed responses for individual MLAs Party preference across caste-based seats Dalit MLAs: Brahmin MLAs: Thakur MLAs: Kurmi MLAs: Yadav MLAs: Other communities Across Lodhi, Jat, Nishad, Gurjar, Maurya, and Rajbhar MLAs, BJP and Samajwadi Party remain the dominant preferred parties, though dissatisfaction with individual MLAs remains high.

stories.title: Jhansi sees heavy rain amid extreme heat:17 districts on storm alert while heatwave warning remains in 35 districts
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh is reeling under extreme heat, with temperatures soaring past 47°C and breaking multiple records over the past 24 hours. Banda emerged as the hottest place in the world, recording a scorching 47.6°C. Previously, the highest temperatures recorded there were 47.4°C on April 30, 2022, and April 25, 2026. Partial Relief as Winds and Rain Activity Begin Despite the intense heat, parts of the state saw some relief on Tuesday morning. Cool winds began blowing across cities like Lucknow and Kanpur, reducing the impact of the harsh sunlight. Late Monday night, Jhansi witnessed heavy rainfall for about 30 minutes. Meanwhile, dust storms swept through Lucknow and Ghaziabad, covering the sky with thick dust clouds. Temperature drops slightly in several regions According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), cooler winds from the eastern direction have caused temperatures to drop by 2–3°C across western and eastern Uttar Pradesh. However, in the Bundelkhand region, temperatures have risen by about 1°C. Storm and Rain Alert in 17 Districts The IMD has issued a warning for thunderstorms, strong winds, and rainfall in 17 districts, including: Wind speeds may reach up to 70 km/h in these areas. See weather pictures In Prayagraj, a laborer was seen unloading earthen pots from a vehicle amidst intense sunlight. Heatwave warning in 35 districts continues Even as rain is expected in several regions, a heatwave alert remains in place for 35 districts, indicating continued extreme weather conditions across the state. Western disturbance to bring further relief Meteorologist Atul Singh from Lucknow said that a new western disturbance has become active, which will trigger a fresh spell of rain accompanied by thunderstorms. He added that temperatures may fall by 2–4°C over the next five days, offering partial relief from heatwave conditions. Weather forecast for the next four days April 29: Widespread rainfall is expected across eastern and western Uttar Pradesh, along with strong winds. Night temperatures are likely to fall. April 30: Rain is likely across the state, with chances of lightning. Hot winds may blow at speeds of up to 40 km/h during the day. May 1: Light rain is expected in western Uttar Pradesh, while eastern regions may receive heavier showers. Thunderstorms and lightning are likely. May 2: Light rainfall may occur in some areas. Strong winds will continue, along with a slight drop in temperature. Mixed conditions: Hot days, warm nights In some parts of the state, heatwave conditions may persist during the day, while nights could also remain unusually warm. However, with the onset of rain and thunderstorms from April 28, temperatures are expected to decline by 2–4°C, improving overall heatwave conditions. Due to the impact of the western disturbance, scattered rainfall activity is likely to begin in western Uttar Pradesh and gradually move toward eastern regions in the coming days.

Dhirendra Shastri says, 'Temples crowded, now need ‘storm’ on streets':Plans Rudrabhishek at Gyanvapi; addresses Hanumant Katha in Prayagraj
stories.summary: The Peethadhishwar of Bageshwar Dham, Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, has a Hanumant Katha (religious discourse) in Prayagraj starting today. He arrived at Bamrauli Airport by helicopter. From here, he traveled by car to Karela Bagh, then reached Arail Selfie Point by steamer on the Yamuna. Upon Dhirendra Shastri's arrival, devotees chanted slogans hailing Bageshwar Baba. A grand pandal (tent) has been constructed over 13,000 square meters at the Katha venue on the Yamuna bank. The three-day Katha is expected to attract over 5 lakh devotees. The pandal has seating arrangements for approximately 20-22 thousand devotees. The entire event is being organized over an area of about six acres. Eight entry gates have been constructed in the pandal for devotees to enter and exit. Surveillance is being conducted with 3000 police personnel along with 500 CCTVs and drones. Among the huge crowd gathered to listen to Dhirendra Shastri's Katha, one devotee has arrived in a wheelchair. See 2 pictures The patron of the Hanumant Katha is BJP leader Dr. Uday Pratap Singh, a resident of Prayagraj. He is the Director of Harinarayan Group of Colleges. He has a total of five colleges. Apart from this, he has a rice mill. His father had a factory in Mirpur. Later, Uday Pratap started doing property business. Dr. Uday Pratap Singh has also met Home Minister Amit Shah several times. He is also close to Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya. He has organized many programs before this as well. These have included Bollywood actress and MP Kangana Ranaut, cricketer Suresh Raina, Bhojpuri actress Akshara Singh, singer Hansraj Raghuwanshi, and many other film artists.

stories.title: Groom’s uncle left behind by baraat in Jhansi:Later found hanging from tree 100 metres from guest house; suicide suspected
stories.summary: In Jhansi, the wedding procession bus moved ahead without the groom's uncle being seated. This made him angry. His daughter and son-in-law persuaded him and stopped the bus to make him board. After this, the wedding procession reached the wedding venue. There, the uncle gave his purse and mobile to his daughter, then went missing. In the morning, his body was found hanging from a tree about 100 meters away from the wedding venue. Family members said that the driver of the bus carrying the wedding procession had stopped the vehicle on the way for some work. The groom's uncle, who was traveling in it, got down to urinate. Meanwhile, the bus started moving. People stopped the bus about 20 meters ahead. However, the uncle refused to board the bus. The matter is from Month town. Know the complete matter in detail Ishwar Singh (57), a resident of Joohi area in Kanpur, was an electrician by profession. His cousin brother Agan Kumar lives in Rajpur in Kanpur Dehat. Agan's son Manoj's wedding was fixed in Jhansi. To attend that wedding, he first went to Rajpur. Then from there, he went to Jhansi on the wedding bus. Ishwar Singh's son Rohit Verma said that the wedding procession left from Kanpur Dehat on Monday evening for Month in Jhansi. When the bus stopped on the way, Papa also got down to urinate. Meanwhile, the bus started moving. When he raised an alarm, the bus was stopped about 15 to 20 meters ahead. He got angry about this. Then his sister and brother-in-law pacified him and made him sit in the bus. At night, the wedding procession reached Pitambara in Month. Disappeared with daughter's purse and mobile Son Rohit said - Father did not go inside the wedding venue. He gave his mobile and purse to sister outside and left. Sister tried to stop him, but he didn't listen. Sister called out, but the DJ was playing so no one could hear. Sister went inside and brought family members, but by then father had already left. After this, a search was started for him, but no clue was found. On Tuesday morning, he was being searched for again. Meanwhile, about 100 meters away from the wedding venue, the father was found hanging from a tree in the bushes with a noose made from a gamcha (towel). After this, people from the surrounding area gathered and informed the police. The police have sent the body for post-mortem. Nephew Yogendra said that uncle Ishwar Singh was mentally disturbed. His treatment was also ongoing. He would get very angry over small matters. This is why he committed suicide. After the suicide, mourning spread at the wedding venue. Family members reached the spot crying and wailing. Ishwar has 2 sons Rohit and Mohit. Neither of them is married, while daughter Neha is already married.

stories.title: PM to inaugurate UP’s first Sowa-Rigpa hospital in Varanasi:Herbal-based treatment to be offered at the new facility
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh's first Sowa-Rigpa hospital is ready. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate it virtually on April 28. He is coming on a 2-day visit to his parliamentary constituency Kashi. The hospital is being spruced up before the inauguration. Painting work has started outside the campus. In this hospital, incurable diseases will be treated with medicines made from herbs. Currently, 5 OPDs are running here daily, which include General Medicine, Gynecology Department, Psychiatry Department, and Pediatrics Department OPDs. On average, 250 patients are reaching here daily for treatment. First know, what is Sowa-Rigpa medical system The Sowa Rigpa medical system is approximately 5,000 years old. Sowa means healing an unhealthy body and Rigpa means science, that is, special knowledge of health. This means it is the science of health. In this clinic, medicines are prepared only from herbs and are being provided to patients at minimal prices. Patients coming to this hospital first need to register for Rs 25. This newly constructed hospital has been built with 45 beds. Arrangements for a minor OT have also been made. The first hospital from where eight MD doctors graduated Varanasi's Sowa Rigpa Medical Institute is the only institution from where the first batch of MD graduates passed out in 2012. Five students are also pursuing PhD which will be completed soon. There are three permanent teachers here, of which one post is vacant. 11 teachers and four medical officers are on contract. Therapy assistants, pharmacists all are on contract. Due to shortage of manpower, there are inconveniences here. Admission to BSRMS is done through NEET. Every year admission takes place for 15 seats. The hospital started with one room 33 years ago Dr. AK Rai, who has been working here for about 25 years, says that the Sowa Rigpa clinic started in a small room in Sarnath, Varanasi in 1993. But today it has been developed as a Medical College and Hospital. In 1996, a course was created here and academic work began. In 2001, the institution received recognition. In 2008, the institution organized a 2-day national level seminar for the first time. After continuous efforts, in 2010, the government recognized it as a separate medical system after it was passed by the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. In 2020, the Ministry of Culture provided a budget to build the Sowa Rigpa Hospital. Due to COVID, there was also a delay in its completion.

stories.title: SC pulls up UP Police over Noida hate crime case:Questions missing IPC 153-B, flags lapses; next hearing on May 19
stories.summary: The Supreme Court of India has expressed strong displeasure over the Uttar Pradesh Police’s handling of the 2021 Noida hate crime case. Questioning the conduct of the investigating officer (IO), the court remarked, “Why is your IO playing hide and seek with this court?” Bench questions missing IPC Section 153-B A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta asked Additional Solicitor General K M Nataraj why IPC Section 153-B—related to statements against national unity—was not added to the FIR. The court noted that Section 295-A, which deals with hurting religious sentiments, had been invoked. Court flags non-compliance with earlier assurance The court pointed out that on February 16, the state had indicated that Sections 153-B and 295-A should be applied based on the complaint. However, 153-B has still not been added. Calling the compliance affidavit unsatisfactory, the bench expressed concern over delays and inconsistencies. During the hearing, the ASG said the trial court has permitted further investigation and assured that necessary sections would be added. However, the petitioner’s counsel claimed that Section 153-B was removed again. Warning to officials, next hearing on May 19 The court considered summoning the investigating officer but granted the state two weeks’ time on request. The next hearing is scheduled for May 19. It also issued a stern warning, asking the state to advise its officials or risk consequences, adding that the court has no interest in summoning and reprimanding them. 2021 incident in Noida’s Sector 37 The case relates to a July 4, 2021 incident in Noida’s Sector 37. The complainant, a Delhi resident travelling to Aligarh for a wedding, was allegedly assaulted due to his beard and Muslim identity. He was reportedly abused and harassed. The petition also seeks action against some Uttar Pradesh Police officials for allegedly failing to comply with Supreme Court directives.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:CM joins women participants in Jan Akrosh rally; JD Vance to visit Pakistan for peace talks more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. JD Vance to depart for Pakistan for second round of peace talks shortly The Vice President of the US, JD Vance, will soon leave for Pakistan to lead the second round of peace talks scheduled in Islamabad on Wednesday. These talks will address issues relating to the Iran war. 2. BJP’s Jan Akrosh Rally in Lucknow: Yogi marches with women; state president blames SP for harming 80% women over 'Naqab politics' The BJP organized a Jan Akrosh Mahila Padyatra (women’s protest march) in Lucknow on Tuesday after the Women’s Reservation Bill failed to pass in the Lok Sabha. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath personally walked alongside women during the march, which saw participation from nearly 15,000 women. 3. Row over smart power meters escalates in UP: Yogi seeks probe report; Akhilesh promises 300 units free electricity Electricity has always been a major political issue in Indian states, and the situation in Uttar Pradesh (UP) is no different. A strong example is Delhi, where the promise of free electricity helped the Aam Aadmi Party secure a massive electoral victory. Even today, several states run subsidized electricity schemes. In Madhya Pradesh, consumers pay just ₹100 for 100 units. Similar schemes exist in Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh. In Uttar Pradesh itself, farmers and weavers already receive subsidized or free electricity. 4. Kharge takes U-turn on his ‘terrorist’ remark about PM Modi At a joint press conference in Tamil Nadu, Mallikarjun Kharge said, “How can AIADMK join with Modi? He is a terrorist. Later, clarifying his statement, he said, "I would like to clarify my remarks about Narendra Modi. 'I never said he is a terrorist, rather, I meant that he is terrorising among people and political parties”. 5. Hindu activists stopped at Lenskart store over tilak push: Protest outside; posters defaced with shoes, police deployed to control situation On Tuesday, there was a major commotion at the Lenskart outlet located in Manas Nagar, Agra. Leaders and workers of a Hindutva organization arrived there to make the employees working there wear kalawa (sacred thread), tilak, kada (bracelet), and turban. 6. ‘Blue Drum case’ accused Muskan brought to court from Jail: Carries 6-month-old daughter in her arms; police also produce co-accused lover Sahil In Meerut's highly publicized Saurabh murder case, accused Muskan and her lover Sahil were presented in court on Tuesday. Both were brought to court from jail amid heavy security. Police first arrived at court with Sahil. He was wearing a white cap and round neck T-shirt. 7. SC in Sabarimala case questions how can deity be defiled by touch? Supreme Court is hearing the case related to women’s entry into the Sabarimala temple and allegations of religious discrimination. The court asked, “How can touching the idol be considered an insult to God?” 8. Akhilesh says, 'BJP is rehearsing for opposition role': Takes jibe at Jan Aakrosh rally; Seema Rajbhar named Mahila Morcha chief Taking a jibe at BJP's Janaakrosh rally in Lucknow, former CM Akhilesh Yadav said, “I heard there was a foot march in Lucknow. In such scorching heat, no one wore dark glasses. This is the first government that is practicing opposition while being in power.” 9. ‘He had no right to live’: Brother reacts after niece’s rape and murder accused killed in encounter Family members of a man accused of raping and murdering his niece refused to claim his body after he was killed in a police encounter in Ghaziabad. Praising the police and the Yogi Adityanath government, they said he “had no right to live.” 10. Pahalgam attack 1st anniversary tomorrow: Baisaran remains closed; Army says 'India has not forgotten anything' 22 April marks the first anniversary of the Pahalgam attack. Security has been intensified across tourist locations in Kashmir, with agencies on high alert. .

stories.title: Newborn cries beside parents' dead bodies in Hardoi:Husband’s head crushes, wife’s spine breaks; bike flung 4 feet into air
stories.summary: A husband and wife riding a bike were killed in a road accident on Tuesday in Hardoi. Their 3-month-old baby slipped from the mother’s lap and fell onto the road. The infant lay on the ground, crying beside her parents’ bodies. The couple was returning from a wedding ceremony on their bike when a speeding car hit them. The impact was so severe that both were thrown nearly four feet into the air and landed at a distance. The husband suffered a fatal head injury, while the wife’s waist bone was broken. The Pulsar bike was completely shattered into pieces in the accident. On receiving information, the police reached the spot and sent the bodies for postmortem. The car driver fled from the scene, and the police are scanning CCTV footage to trace him. The accident took place in the Pachdevra police station area. After the incident, family members reached the spot and were seen crying and clinging to the bodies. The crash was so severe that the bike was completely wrecked. The 3-month-old infant was found lying on the road, crying beside her parents’ bodies. Full details of the case: The deceased have been identified as Siyaram (22) and his wife Neelam (20), residents of Gahabra village under Pachdevra police station limits. The couple was returning from a family function in Nasinagar village of Shahjahanpur along with their 3-month-old baby. They were married on May 11, 2025, and this was their first child. According to eyewitnesses, the accident occurred around 10 am on Tuesday on the service lane of the Ganga Expressway, when a speeding vehicle rammed into their bike. The collision was so intense that both were flung off and fell far onto the road, sustaining critical injuries. Locals immediately informed the police and tried to rush them to the hospital, but both had died by then. Chaos broke out at the scene after the accident, and a large number of people gathered. The incident took place near Seramau village, about 60 km from the district headquarters. The couple’s 3-month-old baby survived the accident. She suffered only minor injuries and has been handed over to the family. Since the incident, the infant has been continuously crying, making the atmosphere even more emotional. Police search for absconding driver The police have launched a search for the absconding driver. The investigation has been intensified, and CCTV footage is being examined. Locals said overspeeding on the expressway service lane is a major cause of such accidents and demanded strict action from the administration. People warned that unless speed control and monitoring are improved, such accidents will continue to claim lives. The station in-charge said a case has been registered and efforts are underway to arrest the accused driver soon.

stories.title: Fake doctor arrested in KGMU Lucknow:Police say, 'He trapped Hindu girls, pushed conversion agenda; ran brainwashing sessions
stories.summary: A fake doctor was caught at KGMU in Lucknow on Tuesday. After presenting the accused before journalists, he was handed over to the police. He is accused of trapping medicos in a love trap and plotting religious conversion. Additionally, he was planning to take female students outside under the pretext of arranging meetings with American doctors at AIIMS Delhi. KGMU spokesperson Dr. KK Singh stated that after the Rameez Malik case that came to light in the Pathology department a few days ago, an investigation team was formed on the Vice Chancellor's instructions. He was given the responsibility of this team. During this period, suspicious activities were being monitored. Conspiracy revealed in investigation Information was received that some people were trying to lure KGMU female students and take them outside. When the team increased surveillance, it was found that there was a plan to take the female students out of Lucknow under the pretext of meeting American doctors at All India Institute of Medical Sciences Delhi. Accused Caught Near Surgery Department According to the spokesperson, the accused has been identified as Hasan Ahmad. He used to pose as a doctor by organizing medical camps in Lucknow. On April 20, during an inspection at one such camp, around 20 KGMU students were found present. When the situation seemed suspicious, the team laid a trap and caught him near the surgery department on Tuesday. Later, the accused was presented at a press conference in Brown Hall and handed over to the police. Used to roam in doctor's attire, had access to multiple departments The accused always wore doctor's attire and had more than 20 male and female students in his contact. He claimed to have access to multiple departments. However, it has not yet been confirmed which staff members he was in contact with. Used fake letterhead and signatures Investigation revealed that the letters given to female students had fake signatures. The accused had prepared fake letterheads in the name of KGMU. The administration has termed this as a major conspiracy and has demanded an impartial investigation by the police. Accused's Confession During interrogation, the accused revealed that he is 12th pass and studied at Shia Inter College in Lucknow. He had formed an organization in the name of social service, through which he organized medical camps. When questioned about coming in contact with female students, he could not give a clear answer. He claimed that four doctors are associated with him and he was about to open a hospital soon. The accused also named people associated with his organization, mentioning some doctors connected to Era Medical College and Integral University. Faiq Ahmed Mansuri has been identified as the main operator of the organization. Investigation Ongoing Currently, the police are investigating the entire matter. KGMU administration has demanded a detailed investigation, considering it a serious conspiracy.

stories.title: Meerut ‘Blue Drum’ Saurabh murder case:Muskan, Sahil produced in court; judge questions duo for over 40 minutes
stories.summary: In Meerut's highly publicized Saurabh murder case, accused Muskan and her lover Sahil were presented in court on Tuesday. Both were brought to court from jail amid heavy security. Police first arrived at court with Sahil. He was wearing a white cap and round neck T-shirt. After getting down from the police vehicle, he lowered his head and kept walking at the officers' signals. Some lawyers tried to stop him, but policemen pushed them back. After this, police personnel took Sahil to court. Shortly after, police arrived with Muskan. She was wearing a yellow printed suit and black dupatta. She had a black mask on her face. She was carrying her 5-month-old daughter in her lap. With her gaze lowered, Muskan entered the court. The baby was also wrapped in the dupatta. There was a police cordon all around, which didn't allow anyone to approach Muskan. On March 18, Muskan was arrested and sent to jail for the murder of her husband Saurabh, and now after about 13 months, she has been seen for the first time. Just before Sahil, Saurabh's mother and brother had also reached the court. They were stopped by the police personnel earlier. In this case, famous as the Blue Drum Case, proceedings under Section 313 have now begun. This means the judge is now directly questioning the accused. The first date of hearing was set for April 15, but due to special reasons, the hearing could not take place that day. After that, the date of April 18 was fixed, but even on that day the process could not be completed. Now the hearing in this case is taking place today, i.e., April 21. First see the pictures of Muskan coming to court Testimony of 22 witnesses completed So far, statements of 22 witnesses have been recorded in the Merchant Navy Officer Saurabh murder case. After these testimonies, the prosecution's evidence has been closed. Now the process under Section 313 will begin in the court. After this, final arguments will take place and then the court will pronounce its verdict. Will respond to charges against himself 22 witnesses have given several important statements in court against Muskan and Sahil, in which both have been accused of murdering Saurabh together. Now based on these testimonies, both the accused will be asked about 15 to 20 questions, which they will have to answer. If the accused are unable to give satisfactory answers to the charges against them, it could go against them. This entire process under Section 313 can last for about 1 to 2 hours. Online hearing for security reasons Generally, under Section 313, the accused has to appear in court and respond, but considering the safety of Muskan and Sahil, their appearance will be conducted through video conferencing. During the previous hearing, lawyers had attacked both of them in the court premises. Similarly, during delivery at the hospital, a crowd had gathered around Muskan. Now know the complete case February 25, 2025 was Muskan's birthday. Exactly one day before, on February 24, Saurabh had come to Meerut to celebrate the birthday. After Saurabh's return, Sahil started becoming disturbed. It was decided that Saurabh had to be eliminated on March 4. Muskan first put Peehu to sleep in the room next to the bedroom. That night, she mixed sedative medicine in the dinner. Saurabh fell asleep quickly after eating. After this, Muskan called Sahil. After Sahil arrived, Muskan stabbed a knife into Saurabh's chest. After Saurabh's death, his body was dragged to the bathroom. Muskan and Sahil together cut the body into 4 pieces. To hide them, they brought a large plastic drum for storing water from the market. The body pieces were filled in this drum.

stories.title: Akhilesh says, 'BJP is rehearsing for opposition role':Takes jibe at Jan Aakrosh rally; Seema Rajbhar named Mahila Morcha chief
stories.summary: Taking a jibe at BJP's Janaakrosh rally in Lucknow, former CM Akhilesh Yadav said, “I heard there was a foot march in Lucknow. In such scorching heat, no one wore dark glasses. This is the first government that is practicing opposition while being in power.” He also took a dig without naming anyone about the inspection of a tea seller's shop in Fatehpur. He said - The tea seller used to say that no one can make tea better than me. Perhaps this was the reason for the displeasure. On Tuesday, the SP chief was addressing a press conference at the SP office. During this, he also announced the new national president of SP Mahila Morcha. Outgoing national president Juhi Singh announced Seema Rajbhar, a resident of Ballia, as the new president. Read Akhilesh Yadav's key statements... 1. BJP is misleading the public SP chief Akhilesh Yadav said- Socialist people have been in favor of women's reservation. If anyone wants to stop reservation, it is the BJP. We will not let their ill intentions succeed. Those who don't want to count know that when the census happens, people will demand a caste census. When there is talk of caste census, people will talk about their rights. That's why BJP's effort was to mislead the public. Now to hide the defeat of their ill intentions, these people are protesting as a show. These people wanted to create division among women but we together stopped them. 2. BJP can do anything when losing Akhilesh said - In Hitler's time, a minister was appointed for propaganda. But in the BJP government, as many people as are sitting in constitutional positions, they are also doing the government's work. BJP can do anything when losing. Now it is losing. When it goes, it will never come back. Those people who can tell such lies, who are roaming on the streets in opposition to a bill that has already been passed. People who have taken oath. They want to serve their own interests by lying. When a young man gave me tea, his shop was shut down. The tea-seller youth used to say that no one can make tea better than me. Perhaps this was the reason for the displeasure. 3. PDA is Gen-Z Responding to the question about Gen-Z's role in PDA, the former CM said - PDA itself is Gen-Z. What was the Bahujan Samaj, that is PDA. For the first time in history, one community is going to defeat one party. The name of that community is PDA family. We all believe that those who have pain, suffering, torture... all together are going to contest against BJP and form a PDA government. 4. Women need protection along with reservation Women need protection along with reservation. Tell me today, what do the statistics show? We and you...all the people here...this young generation of ours must know that views tell you how much you are trending. How many views there are. That tells you what your TRP is. In any class, whoever has the most marks is the topper. Those are the numbers, they tell you who the topper is. Similarly, if we look at the statistics, if women are most unsafe anywhere, it is in UP. It's not one or two incidents, a large number of incidents are happening which are happening continuously and the government is hiding them. They destroyed 1090, destroyed 108 ambulance. 102 was for women's health services, they shut it down. 5. Until now they kept changing names, now their name has changed Akhilesh Yadav said in response to a question - Until now, they were the ones changing names, now someone has changed their name. In West Bengal, there is a different party's government. If they keep talking like this, an FIR might get registered. Actually, it is being reported that in West Bengal, Subhash Chandra Bose's slogan - "Give me blood, I will give you freedom..." was attributed to Swami Vivekananda. On this, TMC MP Mahua Moitra called him bulldozer brain.

stories.title: Hindu activists stopped at Lenskart store over tilak push:Protest outside; posters defaced with shoes, police deployed to control situation
stories.summary: On Tuesday, there was a major commotion at the Lenskart outlet located in Manas Nagar, Agra. Leaders and workers of a Hindutva organization arrived there to make the employees working there wear kalawa (sacred thread), tilak, kada (bracelet), and turban. However, upon receiving information, the police reached the spot before the Hindutva workers and stopped them from entering the outlet. During this, some workers tried to forcibly enter and make the employees wear tilak-kalawa, but the police showed strictness and stopped them. The Hindutva activists could not succeed in their attempt. After not being allowed entry into the outlet, the activists started protesting outside. They threw Lenskart's posters on the road and hit them with shoes. The commotion continued for about half an hour. During this, the activists appealed to passersby and customers not to buy glasses from Lenskart. Their allegation was that the company does not respect Hindu culture. Police pacified all the workers by counseling them. Police have been deployed outside the outlet to prevent any untoward incident. What is the entire matter A month ago, Lenskart company had issued a new policy regarding dress code. In this, employees at Lenskart stores were prohibited from wearing tilak, bindi on forehead, and kalava on hands. After this, protests against Lenskart took place across the country. However, after the protests, Lenskart backtracked. Now the company has issued a new policy. What is the new dress code guideline? According to the new guideline, employees will have to wear company T-shirts, plain dark blue jeans, and closed shoes. Along with this, cultural and religious items such as kada, bangles, mangalsutra, kalava are permitted. Small earrings, nose pins, rings, and chains can also be worn. The guideline also states that religious symbols like bindi, tilak, and sindoor are completely acceptable. Similarly, head coverings like turbans and hijabs are also allowed, provided they are clean and do not interfere with work. The company has also stated that it will maintain a professional environment, cleanliness, and equal treatment of all employees. Employees have also been assured that they can raise their complaints with HR without fear.

stories.title: BJP’s Jan Akrosh Rally in Lucknow:Yogi marches with women; state president blames SP for harming 80% women over 'Naqab politics'
stories.summary: The BJP organized a Jan Akrosh Mahila Padyatra (women’s protest march) in Lucknow on Tuesday after the Women’s Reservation Bill failed to pass in the Lok Sabha. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath personally walked alongside women during the march, which saw participation from nearly 15,000 women. Apart from the Chief Minister, both Deputy Chief Ministers and state BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary, along with several senior party leaders, joined the padyatra despite the intense heat. March covers 2 km from CM residence to the Assembly The padyatra started from the Chief Minister’s residence and proceeded nearly 2 kilometers to the State Assembly. Addressing the gathering there, BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary alleged that the Samajwadi Party and Congress harmed 80% of women due to their political stance. He said there is strong anger among women voters. CM Yogi targets SP and Congress Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath accused both the Samajwadi Party and Congress of maintaining anti-women policies. He said the massive turnout despite the severe heat reflects the anger women feel toward these parties. He further stated: There are only four castes in the country, women, the poor, the youth, and farmers. He also claimed that women associated with the Congress, SP, and their allied parties participated in the rally. He added that the movement would not end with this march but would continue at the booth, mandal, block, and district levels across the state. Water stations and ambulances arranged due to heat Keeping the hot weather conditions in mind, the administration arranged water stations and ambulance services along the route of the padyatra. Women participating in the rally raised slogans such as- ‘Rahul Gandhi Murdabad’, ‘BJP stands for women’s respect’. See pictures Minister Gulab Devi criticises SP and Congress Secondary Education Minister Gulab Devi also addressed the gathering and criticized the Samajwadi Party and Congress, saying: Their condition is like a frog. Whether you seat them on silver or gold platforms, they will still jump into the drain. Women’s reservation cannot be decided on the basis of caste. Ministers and allies participate in the March Along with CM Yogi and both Deputy Chief Ministers, several women cabinet ministers also participated in the padyatra. Leaders from alliance parties were present as well, including Om Prakash Rajbhar, and Ashish Patel. Political observers are viewing the event as a show of strength by the BJP. BJP says protest linked to failure of Nari Shakti Vandan Act BJP organisation general secretary Dharampal Singh said the padyatra was organized after the Nari Shakti Vandan Act failed to pass in the Lok Sabha. He described the proposed legislation as an important step by Prime Minister Narendra Modi toward strengthening women politically. He added that despite seeking support from all parties, the bill could not be passed.

stories.title: Is cooking in aluminium utensils dangerous?:AIIMS doctor warns of kidney, liver risks; controversy deepens over tea served to Akhilesh
stories.summary: On April 16, the Food Department raided a tea shop in Fatehpur district. Shopkeeper Aryan Yadav claimed that officials objected to making tea in an aluminum utensil. Officials stated that making tea in an aluminum utensil is prohibited. This was the same shop where Akhilesh Yadav had tea on February 20. When Akhilesh received news of the raid, he called Aryan to Lucknow and gave him a brass utensil. This raised questions: Does cooking in aluminum utensils really harm health? What diseases can it cause? On this, we spoke to Dr. Shashank Shekhar, Associate Professor, Cancer Department at Gorakhpur AIIMS, and Dr. Kripa Ram, Associate Professor of Chemistry at Banaras Hindu University. In this Bhaskar Explainer, we will find answers to these very questions How harmful is cooking in aluminum utensils, and why? Cooking in aluminum utensils is harmful to health. It is carcinogenic, meaning cancer-causing. Nowadays, utensils with aluminum oxide coating are also available. These are slightly less harmful. However, when these utensils are heated at high temperatures, 'leaching' of that layer begins, meaning metal particles start dissolving in the food. Because of this, the food can become poisonous. What diseases can be caused by eating food cooked in aluminum utensils? Aluminum is a neurotoxic metal, meaning it affects the human nervous system. Its effect occurs in 2 ways. 1. The higher the temperature of the utensil. 2. The longer the food stays in the utensil. The more aluminum leaching will occur. Its presence in food can cause digestive problems. Besides this, it can also cause several serious diseases. Such as- Harmful for kidneys and bones The kidneys work to filter out toxic substances from the body. The body excretes a small amount of aluminum through urine and feces, but high levels of aluminum substances affect kidney function. In people who already have kidney-related problems, aluminum cannot be excreted from their bodies. This can increase toxicity (poisoning) in bones and the brain. The body's ability to absorb calcium decreases, and the risk of ‘osteoporosis’, a disease that weakens bones, increases. Children's growth may be hindered Excessive aluminum intake in the body can affect the brain development of children. This can weaken their memory, learning, and decision-making abilities. Meaning, the progressive power of the brain decreases. Memory loss Long-term use of aluminum utensils can lead to Alzheimer's and dementia, which is memory loss. Additionally, it weakens digestion. Doctors cannot clarify how many years of eating food in aluminum utensils it takes for the damage to become apparent. Is aluminum foil also harmful for packing food? Aluminum foil is more dangerous than utensils. In fact, its layer is very thin. Because of this, leaching is higher. Even if the foil is not heated directly, leaching occurs due to the warmth and steam of the food. Aluminum foil is more dangerous for acidic food (sour). This can spoil the taste and quality of the food. Are cold drinks that come in tetra packaging and cans also harmful? Generally, the use of aluminum in tetra packaging is considered safe because it uses a very thin layer of aluminum (8 times thinner than hair). It does not come into direct contact with food or liquid. Tetrapack's inner layering contains microplastics, but cold drink cans contain aluminum. Canned cold drinks and juices cause more harm. The reason for this is that cold drinks are acidic in nature. This increases the leaching of aluminum. Cold drinks that come in glass bottles are better than cans. What precautions should be taken when cooking in aluminum utensils? Generally, the use of aluminum for cooking or eating should be avoided in any way. However, if you use aluminum utensils, keep these things in mind- If aluminum is so dangerous, why are its utensils used? Due to its low cost, aluminum is most commonly used in making utensils. Additionally, this metal is very durable. This is why people use aluminum utensils more often. Alloy utensils (mixing more than 2 metals, like iron and copper) are more expensive compared to aluminum utensils. These utensils wear out quickly. On the other hand, aluminum can withstand high pressure. The risk of a cooker bursting is low. Which metals are safe for cooking? Iron is the best for cooking. It helps in overcoming iron deficiency in the body. Besides this, utensils made of copper and brass alloys can also be used. Meanwhile, stainless steel is the safest and most durable option.

stories.title: ‘He had no right to live’:Brother reacts after niece’s rape and murder accused killed in encounter
stories.summary: What will we do with such a corpse, who, while alive, committed such a heinous act with his own niece? Many thanks to the police for eliminating him. The government has done a very good job. We are very happy with the Yogi government. We thank the administration and CM Yogi; such a person had no right to live This is what the brothers of 25-year-old Jasim, who raped and murdered his 4-year-old niece in Ghaziabad, have to say. Jasim was killed in a police encounter on the night of April 19. On April 20, family members did not reach the Ghaziabad post-mortem house to collect the body all day. Police officials kept calling the family members. In the evening, Jasim's brothers and family members arrived, but did not take the body. Late in the evening, the police had the body buried in Ghaziabad itself, in the presence of his brothers. About the incident and the encounter Jasim alias Chhotu, raped and murdered his niece on April 11, and then threw the dead body under a car. The girl's family was from Pilkhua, Hapur, while Jasim was from Sisoli village, Muzaffarnagar. Police had announced a reward of 50 thousand on Jasim. DCP Dhawal Jaiswal said, Additional DCP Crime Piyush Singh received information on Sunday night that Jasim was roaming in Ghaziabad's Tila Mod area. Police cordoned off the area. Jasim was seen coming on a bike with his 2 associates. Police asked them to surrender, but Jasim and his associates started firing. Then everyone started fleeing on their bikes. Police also fired in response. During this, a bullet hit Jasim in the chest. He fell to the ground, covered in blood.As soon as Jasim fell, both his companions fled from the spot. After this, the police took the injured Jasim to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. During the encounter, 2 constables, Head Constable Amit and Iqbal, were injured. Meanwhile, Constable Mohit Sharma's bulletproof jacket was hit by a bullet. Jasim, along with his 2 companions, fired 15 rounds. Cousin said to burn or cremate the body Bhaskar spoke to Mehboob, Jasim's cousin, who had come to the post-mortem house. Mehboob said, Jasim was my cousin. Police came to the village on Monday morning, and we learned that the police had killed him in an encounter in Ghaziabad.Before this, our sister had told us that brother Jasim had raped and murdered her 4-year-old daughter. We had told our sister that we are all with you, whatever has happened, sister, please forgive us. We had also gone to our sister's place and said that for the crime he committed, the punishment should be death. Regarding the encounter, Mehboob said, The police finished Jasim as quickly as possible. We are very happy. We don't need his body anymore. The police themselves brought us from Muzaffarnagar. We told the police to burn this body, throw it in a drain, or cremate it. We don't need the body, nor do we need such a brother. We weren't even coming. Mehboob further says, The police and our sister's in-laws told us to come with them. You have no fault. We came at their word. The police can burn him themselves, we have nothing to do with it. We are happy with the Yogi government Step-brother Naseem said, Jasim was my step-brother, we have not come to take the body, nor do we want to take the body. We don't even want to see the face of this criminal. The police did the encounter correctly. My sister had called, she told me that Jasim had taken my daughter. Since then, we were against him. Naseem further said, Many thanks to the police for eliminating him. The government has done a very good job. We are very happy with the Yogi government. Yogi ji tightened the administration, after which the police took action and killed him in an encounter. For this, we want to express our gratitude. May every criminal's eyes be opened by this. May no one do such a thing again. 'Salute to Yogi ji with respect and honour' Jasim was a resident of Sisauli village in Muzaffarnagar. His father, Ikhlaq, had passed away. After the death of his first wife, Ikhlaq remarried. From his first wife, he had three sons: Shamim, Naseem, and Taufeeq. All three reached the post-mortem house. From Ikhlaq's second wife, he had a son, Jasim, and two daughters. Jasim first raped and then murdered his own sister's 4-year-old daughter. Jasim's wife lives in a rented house in Muzaffarnagar with her two children.

stories.title: Row over smart power meters escalates in UP:Yogi seeks probe report; Akhilesh promises 300 units free electricity
stories.summary: Electricity has always been a major political issue in Indian states, and the situation in Uttar Pradesh (UP) is no different. A strong example is Delhi, where the promise of free electricity helped the Aam Aadmi Party secure a massive electoral victory. Even today, several states run subsidised electricity schemes. In Madhya Pradesh, consumers pay just ₹100 for 100 units. Similar schemes exist in Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh. In Uttar Pradesh itself, farmers and weavers already receive subsidised or free electricity. With assembly elections due in about eight months, the controversy over smart prepaid electricity meters is quickly turning into a major political issue. Public protests across the state have pushed political parties into action. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav recently raised the issue during a press conference and announced that if his party forms the government in 2027, it will provide 300 units of free electricity to consumers. The move signals a clear attempt to convert public anger into electoral advantage. BJP MLAs also raise concerns over smart meters Public dissatisfaction over smart prepaid meters has reached electricity offices as well as political representatives’ offices. In Lucknow, residents even gheraoed the office of Mankameshwar Ward councillor Ranjeet Singh. Samajwadi Party MLA Ravidas Mehrotra staged a protest outside the Madhyanchal Electricity headquarters on Gokhale Marg. Interestingly, concerns are not limited to the opposition. BJP MLAs Dr. Neeraj Bora from Lucknow North and Yogesh Shukla from BKT also expressed dissatisfaction and wrote letters to the Energy Minister demanding action. This indicates that the issue has crossed party lines and is affecting even ruling party representatives at the grassroots level. CM Yogi forms committee to Investigate Complaints To address public anger, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath constituted a four-member committee to examine technical complaints related to smart prepaid meters. The committee has been asked to submit its report within 10 days. The report is expected to clarify whether the meters are functioning properly or whether consumers’ complaints about faulty readings and inflated consumption are valid. Meanwhile, installation of new smart meters has been temporarily halted until the committee submits its findings. However, smart prepaid meters are still being installed for new electricity connections. Why is UP power corporation not implementing the CEA ordinance? Officials claim no formal instructions received The Central Electricity Authority (CEA) amended smart meter rules on April 1, 2026, allowing consumers to choose whether they want prepaid or postpaid smart meters. The amendment refers to Section 47(5) of the Electricity Act, 2003, which gives consumers the right to decide the billing mode of their electricity connection. Despite this, the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL) has not implemented the amendment. Power Corporation officials say they have not received formal orders or guidelines from the Uttar Pradesh State Electricity Regulatory Commission regarding implementation. However, Consumer Council President Awadhesh Verma strongly objected to this position. According to him, ignoring central law amounts to a serious violation of Section 47(5) and undermines consumer rights. He argued that electricity companies cannot impose prepaid meters against the wishes of consumers. The Consumer Council has filed a petition before the regulatory commission demanding the implementation of the CEA amendment. The commission sought a response from the Managing Director of the Power Corporation within 10 days. The deadline is set to expire on April 22, and no response has been submitted yet. Energy minister issues relief measures after public complaints After receiving feedback from public representatives and consumers, Energy Minister A.K. Sharma held a meeting with officials and issued five major instructions to reduce consumer hardship: Electricity will not be disconnected for 45 days after installation of a new smart meter. Even if the balance becomes zero, electricity supply will continue for up to three days or ₹200 (for a 2-kilowatt load). A five-stage SMS alert system will be implemented: Electricity will not be disconnected on Sundays, holidays, or at night, even if the balance is negative. Electricity supply must be restored immediately after recharge. These steps are intended to reduce consumer dissatisfaction and prevent further protests. Consumer complaints from Mau, Lucknow and Basti ₹2,000 monthly bill for minimal usage Harish Chandra Chauhan from Sarayganesh in Mau district says his household uses only one fan and three LED bulbs, yet he receives electricity bills exceeding ₹2,000 every month. According to him, even if a 75-watt fan runs continuously for 24 hours, consumption should be around 50–60 units per month. Three LED bulbs consume only 10–12 units monthly. Despite this limited usage, he has been facing high billing for the last seven months. Electricity not restored even after recharge Harshit Gupta from Lucknow said his connection was converted from postpaid to prepaid without his consent. After his balance turned negative, electricity supply was disconnected. Although he recharged the connection, electricity was not restored even after two days. He called the 1912 helpline more than 10 times but received no relief. Smart Meter Installed Instead of Net Meter at Solar Home Poonam Srivastava from Bairiyawan locality in Basti installed a 3-kilowatt rooftop solar system in January. Her connection load is 4 kilowatts. According to rules, she should have received a net meter, which records both imported and exported electricity. Instead, a smart prepaid meter was installed. Her son Ajay Srivastava says their solar system produces about 15 units daily, while consumption is only 10–12 units. Earlier, daily consumption data was visible on the UPPCL consumer app. However, after they complained about the absence of a net meter, daily readings stopped appearing. Now, consumption is shown only after 15 days. As a result, they are forced to recharge ₹1,500–₹2,000 every 15 days. Electricity disconnections trigger statewide protests 70 lakh connections converted without consent Last month, the electricity department converted 70 lakh postpaid smart meter connections into prepaid connections without consumer consent. Security deposits of about ₹2,000 were adjusted into advance balance and consumers were informed through SMS. However, when balances went negative, electricity supply was disconnected. This affected more than 5 lakh consumers, triggering protests across several cities. The situation worsened when electricity supply was not restored even after recharge. Complaints on the 1912 helpline also failed to provide relief. Consumers were repeatedly asked to file complaints again instead of receiving solutions. As frustration increased, protests intensified. Protests across Lucknow and other cities On April 14, more than 500 residents gathered at the Laulai substation in Chinhat, Lucknow and staged a gherao. Bharwara-Malhaur corporator Mamta Rawat joined the protest. Most protestors were residents of Kanshiram Colony. Similar demonstrations were held at: Consumers demanded restoration of postpaid smart meters instead of prepaid systems. Over 40,000 daily applications seeking conversion back to postpaid Electricity offices across Uttar Pradesh are receiving over 40,000 applications every day from consumers requesting conversion back to postpaid billing. Deepak Kumar from Lucknow said his electricity consumption suddenly increased after installation of a smart prepaid meter. His electricity supply was disconnected after the department showed an outstanding amount of ₹9,622. Even after recharge, he received another message asking him to deposit ₹174 more. He questioned how electricity charges could increase further when supply was already disconnected. Due to such experiences, many consumers believe prepaid smart meters are leading to unfair billing and exploitation. As a result, the demand to revert to postpaid smart meters continues to grow rapidly across the state.

stories.title: Rinku Singh visits Kashi Vishwanath temple in Varanasi:Offers prayers with MP-fiancée Priya Saroj; see pictures
stories.summary: Cricketer Rinku Singh visited the Kashi Vishwanath Temple on Tuesday with his fiancée Priya Saroj. The couple offered prayers like common devotees through the Ganga gate before leaving. Rinku had arrived in Varanasi on Monday, where Priya received him at Lal Bahadur Shastri Airport. Dressed in a black T-shirt and trousers, Rinku was greeted by fans seeking selfies and autographs. Priya wore a pink Lucknowi chikankari kurta with blue jeans. From the airport, Rinku headed straight to the Taj Hotel Varanasi. See pictures... Rinku Singh playing for KKR in IPL 2026 Playing for Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR), he delivered victory in Sunday's match against the Rajasthan Royals (RR) in IPL 2026. In the Kolkata-Rajasthan match, he scored an unbeaten 53 runs off 34 balls. He also led the team to a 4-wicket victory. Rinku got engaged to Priya Saroj in 2025, wedding is to take place after IPL India finisher Rinku Singh MP Priya Saroj are engaged. Both are going to take 7 pheras (wedding vows) in June 2026 this year. Last year, Rinku and Priya's ring ceremony took place in Lucknow. Sources say that after the father's demise, the family may reconsider Rinku's wedding date. Earlier, Rinku-Priya's wedding date had been postponed twice. The first date was fixed on November 18, 2025, but it was postponed due to a cricket series. The second date came out in February 2026, but had to be cancelled due to the World Cup. Rinku's elder brother Sonu Singh had informed that the wedding procession will only take place when Rinku is free from IPL. The wedding will be held in Kashi. The reception will be organized in Aligarh. Now read the story of Rinku Singh's struggle Rinku used to get worried seeing Papa work hard Behind Rinku's success was hidden his father's tough struggle. Khanchand used to work as a hawker at a gas agency in Aligarh. For the good upbringing of his 5 sons and daughter, he delivered cylinders door-to-door for many years. Earlier he used to deliver on a bicycle, then he started delivering cylinders to people's homes by tempo. In childhood, Rinku used to get worried seeing his father work so hard. He had promised that Papa...one day I will become your support and relieve you from this hard work. As soon as he became successful in cricket, Rinku also fulfilled his promise made to Papa. His mother Veena Devi takes care of household responsibilities. Rinku is the fourth among 5 brothers and one sister. The elder brothers are Sonu, Mukul and Sheelu. While sister Neha and brother Jeetu are younger than Rinku. His family once lived in Dangarh, Bulandshahr. Which later shifted to Aligarh. Rinku's father said in his last interview - My Son is a star… On the day of the India-Pakistan match on February 15 in the T-20 World Cup, Rinku Singh's father Khanchand spoke to Dainik Bhaskar. He had said that the match was good. My health was a bit poor. But as soon as the four was hit, I started feeling absolutely fine. He had said - I watched the entire match. Rinku is a star. If he had gotten more balls, he would have scored more runs. Rinku had scored 11 runs off 4 balls. He had hit one four and one six. Small scores in big matches are also very helpful, this is a matter of great joy. Family members had said that Khanchand was watching the match on his home TV screen. Seeing Rinku play, he became emotional. After this, he became distressed, remembering Rinku's early days. Then he had said that his son worked very hard to reach this far. But now everything is fine.

stories.title: Heatwave alert issued in 26 districts of UP:State govt changes school timings amid severe heat
stories.summary: Amidst the intense heat in UP, the Yogi government has changed the timings of council schools up to class 8. Basic Education Director Pratap Singh Baghel said that schools up to class 8 will run from 7:30 AM to 1:30 PM. Children will be dismissed at 12:30 PM. Madrassas will also have holidays at the same time. Teachers will remain in school until 1:30 PM. The director has stated that the management committee can decide how long classes will run in private schools. Until now, school timings were from 8 AM to 2 PM. Lucknow DM Vishakh G. Iyer informed that an order to change timings in Lucknow's private schools will be issued on Tuesday. Warning of 5 days of heatwave in UP On Monday, most districts experienced strong sunshine in the morning. The temperature in 27 districts reached 40 °C or more. Hot, strong winds blew in Prayagraj, Varanasi, and Bahraich. Barabanki, Sultanpur, Shahjahanpur, and Hardoi experienced humidity. The streets looked deserted during the day. People who ventured out for essential work were seen protecting themselves with umbrellas and scarves. The Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a heatwave warning for today, Tuesday, in 26 districts, including the Bundelkhand region. It stated that night temperatures would also increase. Yogi appealed to people to take care of themselves by writing a post on 'X'. He said, 'Take special care of children and the elderly. Wear loose cotton or khadi clothes.' Coolers were installed for tigers at Kanpur Zoo. A bear was seen trying to find relief from the heat by rolling in the mud. In the last 24 hours, Prayagraj remained the hottest. The maximum temperature here was recorded at 44.6 °C. The minimum temperature also reached 20 °C. Lucknow's meteorologist, Atul Singh, stated- Due to the effect of an anti-cyclone formed around Maharashtra, the temperature will increase by 2-3C during the next 4-5 days. The temperature in most districts will reach 45C or more. There is a possibility of heatwave in some parts of Eastern UP. Currently, there is no hope of relief from the heat in the remaining days of April. Weather Pictures-

stories.title: Massive fire at ration warehouse in Lucknow:Smoke seen from 2 km away; blaze brought under control after 3 hours
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in a ration warehouse in Lucknow's Madiaon area on Thursday. The fire spread so rapidly that chaos ensued in the entire area within moments. Local residents came out of their homes. High flames and smoke were visible from 2 kilometers away. Three fire brigade vehicles brought the fire under control after a strenuous 3-hour effort. Eyewitnesses stated that as soon as the fire broke out, warehouse employees and local residents tried to extinguish it, but the flames were so intense that it became difficult to control them. The fire brigade was immediately informed thereafter. By the time the fire was extinguished, ration and sacks worth millions kept in the warehouse had turned to ashes. See 4 pictures People took control themselves Due to the narrow lanes of Keshav Nagar, fire engines faced difficulties reaching inside. This caused an initial delay in extinguishing the fire, and the flames spread rapidly. The cause of the fire has not yet been revealed. It is suspected that the accident was caused by a short circuit or a cylinder leak. Fire broke out at 5 more places 1. Spark ignited while cutting iron angle at Parag Dairy: A sudden fire broke out at the Parag Dairy complex in the Hazratganj police station area on Thursday. The fire was caused by a spark that arose while cutting an iron angle. After which, it engulfed the diesel pipe. In no time, the fire spread throughout the complex. Contractors first tried to control the fire themselves, but when it didn't extinguish, they informed the fire brigade. Upon receiving the information, the fire department team reached the spot and started extinguishing the fire. After about an hour of strenuous effort, the fire was brought under control. Two fire brigade vehicles remained deployed at the scene. According to Fire Station Officer Ram Kumar Singh, a person named Prakhar was given the task of scrubbing. During the work, the diesel pipe suddenly caught fire, causing the flames to spread rapidly. However, the fire brigade team brought the situation under control in time. During the incident, media personnel were prevented from entering the premises. Meanwhile, some people arrived at the scene in a Thar vehicle, blaring a hooter, and their vehicle had an expired assembly pass. 2. Fire at Prayagraj Tower: A sudden fire broke out in Prayagraj Tower, located opposite Saryu VIP Guest House in Hazratganj. The fire in this approximately 7-story tower caused chaos. Around 6 PM, smoke was first seen rising from inside the building. Shortly after, the fire alarm started ringing, after which people present in the office panicked, immediately ran outside, and evacuated the building. IDFC First Bank's loan center operates on the ground floor of Prayagraj Tower, while the Times of India office is on the first floor, Navbharat Times on the second floor, and Times Now on the third floor. As soon as the incident was reported, fire brigade vehicles reached the spot. However, one vehicle got stuck in a tangle of electric wires right at the building's gate. The vehicle remained stuck there for about half an hour, which delayed extinguishing the fire. 3. Fire in the bank's basement in Vikas Nagar: A fire suddenly broke out at 6 AM on Thursday in the basement of Ajit Tower Building near Mama Chauraha in Vikasnagar. The fire erupted in the scrap kept under the staircase, filling the entire basement with smoke. Due to the fire, the scrap material kept in the basement was burnt. As soon as the information was received, the Indira Nagar Fire Station team reached the spot. Firefighters quickly took action and brought the fire under control. The relief was that no casualties occurred in this incident. Due to the fire, smoke had filled the basement, which the fire brigade team removed by opening doors and through ventilation. SBI Bank operates on the ground floor of Ajit Tower, while the upper floors have residential flats. Due to the promptness of the fire team, the bank and apartments were completely saved. 4. Gas cylinder caught fire while cooking: A ceremony was being organized in a park located in front of Rajnikhand Power House. During the event, around 12 AM, a gas cylinder suddenly caught fire while cooking. Upon receiving the information, a fire tanker from Alambagh Fire Station reached the spot and completely extinguished the fire. Timely action prevented major damage. 5. Fire in Slums: A fire was reported in the slums near Jalalpur Railway Crossing in the Talkatora area at around 1:30 AM. The fire was spreading rapidly, and there was a risk of nearby shanties also catching fire. Under the direction of Chief Fire Officer Ankush Mittal, two fire tenders from Alambagh were dispatched to the spot under the leadership of In-charge Fire Officer Dharampal Singh. Firefighters reached the spot and started a two-pronged operation to extinguish the fire, bringing it completely under control in about 30 minutes. Due to the promptness of the fire team, the fire was prevented from spreading to nearby shanties. No casualties were reported in either incident.

stories.title: 'People were burning alive, we could only watch helplessly':Witness recalls horror; 8 of one family killed in Mirzapur road crash
stories.summary: In Jigna village of Mirzapur, 8 funeral pyres will be lit simultaneously. The house where preparations for a celebration were underway just a day before is now engulfed in sorrow. Tents and chairs are still set up at the house's entrance. The women of the house are weeping inconsolably. The child's grandmother is unconscious. Eyewitness Hanslal Verma recounts the incident: "The vehicle was burning fiercely. People trapped inside the Bolero were screaming amidst the flames, pleading for help. We stood helplessly 10 meters away, watching. As the heat of the fire intensified, their helplessness became unbearable to watch. They struggled inside, making futile attempts to break the glass. And in a short while, one by one, they all succumbed to death." After some time, the police arrived. The fire brigade team arrived. After much effort, the fire was brought under control. The Bolero was completely burnt. Due to the earlier collision, the 13-foot Bolero had been crushed to half its size. The people burnt alive inside the vehicle could not be identified. Only charred bones remained. The police collected the remains of the bodies and sent them for post-mortem. Actually, Arun Singh's son Shiva, after getting his head tonsured from Maihar Dham, was returning home with 8 family members in a Bolero late Wednesday night. Just 60 km before home, in Dramandganj on the Mirzapur-Rewa National Highway, a speeding truck hit them hard. After that, it collided with several vehicles and caught fire. In the accident, all 8 people, apart from the Bolero driver, were burnt alive. See pictures Silence has spread throughout the entire village. No one cooked in their homes. The entire village is mourning. People trapped in the car were banging on the glass According to Hanslal, people kept burning amidst the flames. The fire continued to burn for two and a half hours. All the occupants of the Bolero were badly burnt. Only their bones were visible. After three to four hours of effort, the police collected all the bodies and sent them for post-mortem in black polythene bags. Grandmother faints while crying On Thursday, the bodies of 8 people arrived home simultaneously. As soon as the bodies arrived, there was an uproar in the house. Shiva's grandmother kept fainting while crying. The father locked himself in a room. He was crying. When the police arrived, they somehow managed to get him out. He could only say, "I wish I was also in the car. What will I do living without my wife and child?" In the accident, Shiva's uncle Pankaj Singh, his wife Veena Singh, and their two children Piyush and Sonam, his aunt and her son also burned alive in this accident. Father Arun Singh said - his younger brother will perform everyone's last rites. He will light the pyre for everyone. Son was born after 7 years of prayers Arun Singh of Jigna village was not having a child even after 7 years of marriage. It was about 8 years ago when, after 7 years of prayers, a child's cry echoed in the house. His aunt had prayed for the child. When the child Shiva turned 8, family members went to Maihar Dham on Wednesday to perform his head-shaving ceremony to fulfill a vow. Father Arun said - preparations for a feast were underway at home. That's why they stayed back. Shiva's mother Vandana, one brother, his wife, my sister, and 3 nephews/nieces had also gone with Shiva. They were returning after the head-shaving ceremony when the accident occurred. According to the police, a speeding truck went out of control after its brakes suddenly failed. The truck collided with a Bolero and a Swift car that were traveling ahead. Both vehicles then crashed into a trolley moving in front of them. Due to the high speed, the Bolero was thrown off after the collision. It caught fire with a loud explosion. Meanwhile, the Swift car got trapped between the truck and the trolley. The fire was so fierce that the 9 occupants of the Bolero did not get a chance to escape. Among them were 8 members of the same family and a driver. The Bolero continued to burn fiercely for about two and a half hours.
