stories.title: UV radiation reaches dangerous levels in UP:15 minutes in sun can burn skin, experts warn of DNA damage
stories.summary: Severe heat across the country, coupled with clear skies, is allowing ultraviolet radiation to reach the Earth directly. In many cities of Uttar Pradesh, including Banda, Prayagraj and Lucknow, radiation levels are high. Staying in direct sunlight for more than 15 minutes in these areas can cause skin burns (sunburn). Experts believe it can also damage our DNA. In such a situation, it is important to understand what ultraviolet radiation is, what the radiation levels are in UP districts, and how the damage caused by it can be prevented. Read Bhaskar’s explainer… Question – What is ultraviolet radiation? Answer – Ultraviolet (UV) radiation consists of rays emitted by the Sun that are invisible to the human eye. However, they can harm our body and skin. According to experts, this radiation is necessary for the body to produce Vitamin D. But prolonged exposure to it increases the risk of sunburn (skin burning due to sunlight), cataracts and skin cancer. Question – Which cities face the highest UV radiation risk? Answer – Uttar Pradesh is witnessing intense heat across the state. Due to clear skies, the Sun’s rays are reaching the ground directly without obstruction. As a result, ultraviolet radiation remains at dangerous levels in several districts of UP. According to weather website Toutempo, UV radiation is at 8 or above in most districts of UP. The highest risk is in Bundelkhand districts. In Banda, Jhansi, Lalitpur and Mahoba, UV radiation has reached 10, indicating an extremely dangerous level of exposure. Question- Where is the risk of UV radiation highest? Answer- The threat of UV radiation is highest in India’s southern and hilly states. Southern states are closer to the Equator. During summer, the Sun’s rays fall more directly there, increasing the risk of ultraviolet radiation. Apart from this, in mountainous regions, the threat of ultraviolet radiation rises by 10 to 12%. Thin air and lower ozone density are unable to block radiation effectively. Snow-covered peaks reflect UV rays like a mirror, doubling their impact. This is why UV radiation remains high in Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Ladakh and Sikkim. Question- Does the ozone layer not block UV radiation? Answer- Ultraviolet rays coming from the Sun are of three types – UV-A, UV-B and UV-C. The ozone layer cannot block UV-A radiation, and nearly 100% of it reaches the Earth. This type is less dangerous than the other two forms of UV radiation. However, UV-A penetrates deep into the skin and can cause premature ageing, including wrinkles, loose skin and sunburn. Only 5% of UV-B radiation reaches the Earth, while the ozone layer blocks the remaining 95%. UV-B exposure can lead to diseases such as skin cancer and cataracts. The ozone layer absorbs 100% of deadly UV-C radiation, not allowing even a single ray to reach the Earth. Exposure to UV-C can instantly destroy living cells in the body. In this way, the ozone layer blocks nearly 90% of the Sun’s harmful radiation, allowing only 10% to reach the Earth’s surface. Question- How can we protect ourselves from UV radiation? Answer- Skin specialist Dr Jangid says UV radiation is strongest between 10am and 4pm. Direct exposure to sunlight should be avoided during these hours. While stepping out, apply sunscreen with a Sun Protection Factor (SPF) of 30 or above. The SPF number indicates how long the sunscreen can protect you in the sun. For example, if you apply sunscreen lotion with SPF 30, it can keep you protected for 30x10, or 300 minutes. Apart from this, people should also wear full-sleeved clothes, a hat and sunglasses.

stories.title: Severe heat grips UP, bathtub installed in government hospital:Banda hottest at 46.8°C, heatwave alert in 60 districts, rain warning in 14
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh is in the grip of severe heat. It is feeling like June heat in April itself. The mercury has crossed 47°C. Bright sunshine has been out since Monday morning. Strong winds are blowing amid movement of clouds in the sky. Blasts of hot winds have made it difficult for people to step out of their homes. The number of patients suffering from vomiting and diarrhoea has increased in hospitals due to the heatwave. A cold room has been set up at a government hospital in Kashi. Four separate beds have been arranged for heat stroke patients. A bathtub has also been installed in the ward. Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 14 districts in the state. At the same time, a heatwave warning has been issued for 60 districts. The weather department says the weather will start changing in the state from today. The spell of rain will begin in western UP and will gradually move towards eastern UP. This is expected to bring some relief from the heat and hot winds. Talking about the last 24 hours, Banda remained the hottest place in the state for the second consecutive day at 46.8°C. Before this, on Saturday, Banda was the hottest place in the world, with the temperature recorded at 47.4°C. Meanwhile, Lalitpur witnessed a strong dust storm followed by heavy rain on Sunday afternoon. Lucknow's meteorological scientist Atul Singh said- There is a possibility of heatwave conditions during the afternoon across the state today, while some places may also witness warm nights. After a fresh western disturbance becomes active, a new spell of rain accompanied by thunder and lightning will begin from tomorrow. Temperatures may fall by 2-4°C over the next five days. Some relief from the heatwave is also expected. See pictures of the weather What will the weather be like for the next 5 days?

stories.title: CM Yogi says UP’s farm growth hits 18%:Record paddy and potato output; International Potato Centre to open in Agra
stories.summary: At a major agriculture conference in North India, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said the state’s farm growth has more than doubled in recent years. He said the growth rate has risen from 8% to 18%, adding that farmers’ hard work and government policies have helped the state become a top producer of several crops. Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chauhan also attended the event held in Lucknow on April 24. The programme saw participation from agricultural scientists, farmer-producer groups, and progressive farmers from nine states and union territories. Lab technology now reached directly to the fields The Chief Minister said that earlier policies were limited only to papers and offices, but now 'lab to land', meaning laboratory technology, is being directly brought to the fields. He informed that in 2017, there were only 69 Krishi Vigyan Kendras (Agricultural Science Centers) in the state, most of which were about to close. Today, their number has increased to 89. These centers are now working as 'Centers of Excellence', where scientists themselves are going to farmers and providing them information about new techniques and seeds. Record Set in Paddy and Potato Production The Chief Minister stated through figures that currently, Uttar Pradesh is producing 425 lakh metric tons of wheat, 211 lakh metric tons of paddy, and 245 lakh metric tons of potatoes. Expressing happiness, he said that with the help of the International Rice Research Center in Varanasi, paddy yield in some areas of the state has now reached up to 100 quintals per hectare, which was very low earlier. Additionally, potato farmers will get even better prices for their crops from the International Potato Center, which will soon start in Agra. Focus on Value Addition for Economic Strength The Chief Minister emphasized the need to not limit farming to mere production but to connect it with the market and industry. He said that to increase agriculture's share in Uttar Pradesh's economy again, the government is now emphasizing 'value addition', i.e., the processing of products. This will not only prevent crop wastage but also enable farmers to get many times more value for their produce. The government's goal is to establish a strong synergy between manufacturing and agriculture, so that new employment opportunities can be created in rural areas themselves and farmers can establish their identity as entrepreneurs. 'Road Map' essential to increase farmers' income Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan praised Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's work, stating that UP has created a new history of development. He emphasized that every state should prepare a 'road map' for farming according to its climate and soil. He informed that the work of creating 'Farmer IDs' is now progressing rapidly in the country, which will enable farmers to directly and easily avail the benefits of government schemes. The Chief Minister also expressed confidence that suggestions emerging from such conferences will bring significant changes in the lives of farmers. Every Farmer Will Have Their Own Digital Identity Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan specially emphasized the utility of 'Farmer ID' at the conference. He said that the central government is rapidly working on creating a unique digital identity for farmers across the country, which will save them from repeatedly going through paperwork. Through this ID, benefits of government schemes like fertilizers, seeds, and subsidies will reach their accounts directly and transparently. Praising the fertile land of UP and its hardworking farmers, he said that the soil and climate of the state are the basis of the country's food security, therefore, working by creating a solid 'Agriculture Road Map' according to the geographical conditions of each district is the need of the hour.

stories.title: ‘He used to be naughty,’ says mahant:Boy thrashed to death in Lucknow gurukul days after admission
stories.summary: An 11-year-old boy was beaten to death at a Gurukul in Lucknow, with the accused Mahant confessing to hours of brutal assault after getting frustrated with the child’s behaviour. The incident took place on April 21, just days after the boy had joined the Gurukul. The accused, Saurabh Mishra alias Kanhaiya (27), who runs Ramanuj Bhagwat Ved Vidya Peeth, told police that the child, Divyansh, was unable to follow the Gurukul’s traditions and remained mischievous throughout the day. He said the boy’s behaviour had worsened over the last 3–4 days, which made him increasingly angry. In his confession, Mishra admitted that he punished the child by making him stand barefoot in the sun for hours. He then beat him through the night using slaps, slippers, kicks and punches. He also forced the child to remove his clothes and hit him on the back with sticks. He further told police that he kicked the boy so hard that he fell and his head hit a wall. After that, he pressed the boy’s mouth and punched him repeatedly on the back, leaving him unconscious. When he checked, the boy had died. The accused then took the body and left it outside the child’s house in Gauria village in Kanpur’s Maharajpur area before fleeing from the spot. Divyansh’s father, Narendra Kumar Dwivedi, had admitted him to the Gurukul on April 15. The accused is also the child’s maternal uncle. After the boy’s funeral on Thursday, police registered a case based on the father’s complaint and arrested Mishra along with his girlfriend, Harshita Soni (23). Both are originally from Chhatarpur and were living on rent in Lucknow’s Para area. During questioning, the accused made several shocking revelations about the incident. Police are now investigating the exact sequence of events and the role of the girlfriend in the case. 'Divyansh used to dance in the Gurukul, all the children were becoming like him' Police interrogated the accused uncle and his girlfriend. The statements they gave left even the officers stunned. The uncle told the police - Divyansh was not following the rules of the Gurukul. He used to make noise in class. He used to talk to other children. He would sing, dance. Seeing his mischief, other children also started adopting his ways within a few days. Seeing this, I started getting annoyed with him. Because of this, I had been brutally beating Divyansh for three days. They used to make him stand barefoot in the sun and beat him with sticks Saurabh confessed that he would strip Divyansh's clothes in the scorching sun and make him stand barefoot on the roof. If he ran towards the shade, he would beat him. All children except Divyansh were given food. If he cried from hunger, he would be beaten with sticks. 'He was beaten on Tuesday night, and in the morning, he was found dead.' The accused uncle stated that on Tuesday night around 9 PM, all the children went to sleep in the room. I was so annoyed with Divyansh that I decided to beat him all night. When I started taking him to an isolated place, he began to scream, which further enraged me. I hit him with slaps, kicks, punches, a stick, a belt whatever I could find. When he cried, I dragged him and slammed him against the wall, causing an injury to his head. That day, I don't know what happened to me, but I didn't even consider his condition during the beating. He fell unconscious after the beating. I left him and went away. In the morning, I saw that he had died. Girlfriend supported, broke CCTV cameras Saurabh said- As soon as the news of Divyansh's death spread, all the children of the Gurukul gathered. I called my girlfriend Harshita Soni, who lived on rent near the Gurukul. She sent all the children to their respective homes. She broke the CCTV cameras installed in the premises. She booked a car for me. I threw Divyansh's body near his house from the car and fled. When the police checked the DVR, they found footage of such brutality with Divyansh that the police officers were stunned. Mess footage showed - all children eating, Divyansh crying in the corner ADCP Anjali Vishwakarma said that the footage of the past three days was shocking. The footage revealed that the accused Saurabh had been brutally beating him for three days. Saurabh would punish Divyansh for hours by making him raise his hands in the scorching sun. All children were being given food in the mess, but Divyansh was punished by being kept hungry. The mess footage clearly shows children eating, while Divyansh is seen crying and wailing in the corner. Dragged by the hair for eating food ACP Chakeri Abhishek Pandey said- It came to light in a footage, in which Divyansh was seen secretly eating his companions' food. Upon realizing this, Saurabh reached the mess in anger. He dragged Divyansh out by his hair. After this, he slapped and punched him repeatedly. DCP East Satyajeet Gupta said- The operator Saurabh Mishra alias Kanhaiya had beaten the child for not obeying something. He has admitted this during interrogation. His girlfriend tried to destroy evidence from the Gurukul. Both have been arrested, 11-year-old Divyansh was beaten to death by his maternal uncle. (File photo)His father was a mahant, used to beat him similarly for mistakesThe Gurukul's operator and accused Saurabh Mishra alias Kanhaiya told the police that they are two brothers. Both are mahants. Their father Suresh Chandra Mishra was also a mahant. For mistakes, their father used to beat both brothers a lot. Therefore, when children make mistakes or don't listen, he also can't tolerate it. On Tuesday night, he beat Divyansh for his mistake. He told the police that he used to beat other children of the Gurukul in the same way.SP's delegation met the victim's familyOn Friday afternoon, the SP delegation reached to meet the victim's family.On Friday, an SP delegation reached the victim's family's home to meet them, which included MLA Amitabh Bajpai, Naseem Solanki, Hasan Roomi, former MP Rajaram Pal, and several other leaders. The delegation gathered complete information about the incident from the family members and assured them that a detailed report would be prepared and submitted to National President Akhilesh Yadav.SP leaders assured the family of all possible help and described the incident as very tragic. Naseem Solanki said that the government talks about 'zero tolerance', so strict action should be taken against the culprits of this incident. He questioned whether bulldozer action would be taken on the properties of the accused.

stories.title: ‘Mere Ram Aaye Hain’:Women break down on seeing Arun Govil; MP visits Meerut Central Market on day 15 of protest
stories.summary: MP Arun Govil reached the ongoing traders' protest in Meerut Central Market. Friday marks the 15th day of the protest. As soon as they saw him, the men and women present at the protest started crying and wailing. While crying, they joined hands and started singing - My God has come, my Ram has come. To this, Arun Govil said - I am not God, I am your brother. You people are my family. These women are my sisters. He said that when you ask for something from God, you don't see whether it is good or bad. We have to pray to God that whatever is good for us should happen. What will happen in this matter, how will it happen, when will it happen? Nobody knows anything about this. Therefore, pray to God. Arun Govil talked to the traders for a long time. He explained a lot to them. After this, the traders postponed their protest. Arun Govil said that it is the order of the Honorable Supreme Court. According to that, we and Awas Vikas (Housing Development) will have to work. But, the government is continuously taking cognizance of you people. You will definitely get justice. Govil said - I have spoken to the Chief Minister and lawyers Arun Govil told the women - it's not that I have come today after 15 days, so I don't know anything about this matter. I have continuously spoken to Supreme Court lawyers and even the Chief Minister regarding this matter. Our side will be presented strongly in the Supreme Court and we will get justice. He said - don't make me a leader, I am your brother When Arun Govil reached among the women for talks, some people present there started shouting slogans of 'Zindabad'. On this, the MP said, 'Don't make me a leader by shouting slogans. I am fine being a brother to these people.' However, despite this, people chanted 'Jai Shri Ram'. Attempt to step out of Ram's character MP Arun Govil is continuously being trolled by the opposition in the name of Ram. Along with this, people also say, "We brought Ram, now what is all this happening to us?" In such a situation, to distance himself from that character, the MP had to say, "I am not Ram."

stories.title: UP government takes major step on smart meters:Electricity won’t be cut for 30 days; despite negative balance
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has given relief to electricity consumers using smart prepaid meters. If a house has a 1-kilowatt connection and the balance becomes negative, the power supply will not be cut for 30 days. Consumers with two-kilowatt connections have also been given relief. If the balance is minus 200 rupees, the electricity will not be disconnected. Energy Minister Arvind Kumar Sharma said, Instructions have been given to officials in this regard. This will provide great convenience to small domestic consumers who often cannot pay their bills on time due to financial difficulties or other reasons. 5-Step SMS Alert System Implemented Energy Minister Arvind Kumar Sharma has clearly stated that even if your electricity bill balance goes negative, your connection will not be disconnected before the completion of a full one-month cycle. Now, the electricity department has launched a new 5-step SMS system. This means you will be alerted 5 times via message before your connection is disconnected, giving you time to pay the bill. Relief has also been provided to small connection consumers with 2 kW capacity. Even if their balance goes negative by up to 200 rupees, their connection will not be disconnected. The same rule of 5 SMS alerts will apply to them as well. Considering the summer, the government is paying special attention to the power system. The minister has instructed officials to increase monitoring. He informed that so far, about 30 lakh new electricity poles have been installed in the state and the capacity of transformers has also been increased. The government says that Uttar Pradesh has now become one of the states supplying the most electricity in the country, and people will not be allowed to face power shortages in this scorching heat. Why did the government need to do this? Actually, a report was recently filed by the Power Corporation with the regulatory commission. According to the report, from March 13 to April 10, 2026, 40.27 lakh smart prepaid meter electricity consumers had their connections disconnected due to a negative balance. Out of these, 24.14 lakh recharged. 22.21 lakh connections were reconnected within two hours. Meanwhile, 1.93 lakh connections could not be reconnected within two hours. Until now, the Power Corporation was claiming that there was a delay in connecting a few consumers' connections due to technical reasons, but its report made it clear that about eight percent of consumers, compared to the total consumers, could not get electricity within two hours of recharging. Consumer Council Demanded Compensation The State Electricity Consumer Council demanded from the Regulatory Commission that those consumers who did not receive electricity supply within two hours should be immediately compensated. Because according to the commission's rules, if electricity is not received within two hours of recharging, the consumer is entitled to receive compensation at the rate of 50 rupees per day. Therefore, the commission should enforce its rule and ensure consumers receive compensation. He also said that the Power Corporation has stated that no consumer has sought compensation. This is completely false. Because when compensation is sought on 1912, no response is given to the consumers. Therefore, the regulatory commission should take suo motu cognizance and ensure that all 1.93 lakh electricity consumers receive compensation of at least Rs 50 per day. So that such an incident does not recur. What is the difference between prepaid and postpaid meters? This is exactly like your mobile SIM's prepaid and postpaid. Just like a prepaid SIM, you have to recharge first to use it. Only after that can you make calls or send messages. All services stop when the balance runs out. Similarly, in a prepaid smart meter, you have to recharge first. As soon as the recharge runs out, the electricity is cut off. You can view real-time electricity consumption, balance, etc., through the smart meter app. No security money deposit is required for this meter. On the other hand, in a postpaid meter, the bill comes at the end of the month. You can view daily electricity consumption on the smart meter app, but payment is only made when the bill is issued. For such connections, a security deposit of 2 thousand rupees has to be made.

stories.title: Sanskrit Board announces exam results:Srishti Dixit of Kannauj tops 10th, Rajneesh Yadav of Pratapgarh tops 12th
stories.summary: The results of the Uttar Pradesh Secondary Sanskrit Education Council's 2026 board examinations were declared on Friday. In Purva Madhyama II (10th), Srishti Dixit from Kannauj became the state topper by securing 94.43% marks. Khushboo Saroj became the second topper with 94.29% marks. Mulayam Singh Yadav and Priyanka Saroj secured 93.29%-93.29% marks. Both jointly stood third. All three are residents of Pratapgarh. In Uttar Madhyama II (Class 12), Rajneesh Yadav topped the state by securing 89.36% marks. Vanshika Srivastava is in second place with 85.64% marks. Kajal and Sanskriti stood third by securing 85.43%-85.43% marks. Rajneesh, Vanshika, and Kajal are residents of Pratapgarh. Sanskriti is a resident of Amroha. Results released simultaneously According to the information provided by the council, results for Purva Madhyama II (Class 10), Uttar Madhyama I (Class 11) and Uttar Madhyama II (Class 12) for all classes were released simultaneously. The results were declared from the camp office of the Directorate of Education located in Lucknow. Students can view their results online on the council's official website www.upmssp.com. This year, the Sanskrit Board examinations were conducted at 241 centers across the state between February 19 and February 28. 95% of candidates passed in Purva Madhyama II (10th) A total of 21,915 candidates were registered for the Purva Madhyama Second Examination, including 21,107 institutional and 808 private candidates. A total of 16,615 candidates appeared in the examination, of which 15,941 were institutional and 674 were private candidates. A total of 15,029 candidates passed, including 14,429 institutional and 600 private candidates. The pass percentage of institutional candidates is 95.96 and the pass percentage of private candidates is 94.78. The total pass percentage is 95.91. In the examination, 11,340 boys and 3,689 girls passed. The pass percentage of boys is 95.68 and the pass percentage of girls is 96.64.

stories.title: ‘She is my girlfriend, she will go with me’:Lover stops bride and groom’s car in Ambedkar Nagar; husband forced to go back
stories.summary: In Ambedkar Nagar, after the farewell, a lover stopped the bride's car, which was on its way to her in-laws' house, in the middle of the road. In a filmy style, he parked his bike in front of the car. He opened the car door, pulled out the bride and groom, and then, pulling the bride towards him, said - 'She is my girlfriend, she is coming with me.' The groom was stunned by the young man's actions. In anger, he confronted him. But the lover started showing photos that he kept on his mobile as proof. He said - 'No one can separate us.' The bride was shocked by the lover's actions. Meanwhile, in anger, the groom called his family and in-laws. When both parties arrived at the scene, a commotion began. The lover was not ready to back down under any circumstances. Showing two years' worth of photos with the girl, he insisted on taking her with him. Seeing the situation escalate, the police were informed. A panchayat (local council meeting) was held all day. After learning everything, the groom's side broke off the marriage and decided to return without the bride. The family members took the girl to the village, and based on the complaint, the police booked the lover for disturbing the peace. The matter is from Saidpur Rajjipur village, Aliganj police station area. Now know the full story Dinesh (27) lives with his mother and sister in Gosaiganj, Ayodhya. His father has passed away. The family had arranged Dinesh's marriage about 6 months ago with Mahima, daughter of Parshuram, a resident of Saidpur Rajjipur village in Ambedkar Nagar district. On April 22, Dinesh arrived at Mahima's house with his wedding procession. After the wedding rituals were completed, the farewell took place the next morning. On Thursday morning, after the farewell, Dinesh left for Ayodhya with his wife Mahima by car. Dinesh had only traveled a few kilometers from his in-laws' house when a young man arrived with 6-7 companions. He stopped the car by parking his bike in front of it. The young man opened the car door. Then he made Dinesh and Mahima get out. My name is Ranvijay, this is my girlfriend... After getting the bride and groom out of the car, the young man said, "My name is Ranvijay." As soon as he said this, he pulled Mahima towards him and said, "She is my girlfriend." The groom was shocked. He confronted the young man, but the young man took out his mobile and started showing some photos. After this, he threatened, saying, "She is coming with me. Tell whoever you want to tell. No one can separate us." When family members arrived, the commotion began The distressed groom called his family and in-laws and gave them all the information. Within about 10 minutes, the bride's family members arrived at the scene. A commotion began. Ranvijay also showed mobile photos to the family members. He showed photos of himself with the girl from the past two years. After seeing the photos, an argument broke out between both parties. Dinesh called the police on 112. Everyone was brought to the police station. The panchayat (council/mediation) continued throughout the day. The groom's side, angered by the discussion of the lover and the bride's relationship in the panchayat, broke off the wedding. The groom refused to take Mahima with him. Then a compromise was reached, and the groom returned without the bride. The relatives took the bride with them. Meanwhile, after a complaint from the bride's side, the police booked the lover boy for disturbing the peace. Both parties mutually agreed to break off the wedding Aliganj Kotwal Bhupendra Kumar Singh said- The groom's side and the bride's side had reached a mutual agreement outside the police station. They gave in writing that they do not want any legal action. The police have challaned the lover for disturbing the peace.

stories.title: Akhilesh claims Deputy CM ran away on Shankaracharya’s visit:Questions law and order in UP; makes sharp remark
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav again questioned the treatment meted out to Shankaracharya on Friday. He said, "Everyone saw how he was treated. What all was not said about Batuk. Later, claims were made of washing his feet and prostrating. But when Shankaracharya arrived, the Deputy CM fled Lucknow. They have ruined the entire health department." On Union Home Minister Amit Shah's statement about straightening the goons of West Bengal by hanging them upside down, Akhilesh said- "Look at their language. Are goons only in West Bengal? Are there fewer goons in Uttar Pradesh, who are roaming freely, sitting on chairs? They should also be hung upside down and straightened." During a press conference in Lucknow, Akhilesh alleged that this government is in the hands of undemocratic people. SP workers are being subjected to injustice. BJP has nothing to do with anyone. Attempts are being made to defame SP. This is a fight to save the constitution. Key points from the SP chief's press conference 1. 'Socialist people are being targeted selectively' Akhilesh said - Crime has increased in UP. What happened in Hathras? The daughter of the Valmiki community did not get justice. The police and the government did not allow the family's last wish to be fulfilled. Can any Sanatani do such a thing? Every political party came forward for justice, but the government did not care about anyone. Socialist people are being selectively targeted. If we have to take a big decision, we will not back down. 2. 'BJP is working as a land mafia' Akhilesh said - BJP is working as a land mafia. Wherever a scheme comes, BJP people acquire the land beforehand. All ponds have been encroached upon. Tell me, the Green Corridor is worth 7000 crores. Green Corridor means where traffic should never stop. But, look at the design. It seems that when the engineer brought the design, the Chief Minister must have thrown the design away and started making the design himself. You must have seen the statue of the lion. It seems that its engineer and guide must also be the CM. 3. 'If you do wrong, the public will stand against you' Akhilesh said - Mamata Banerjee is going to achieve a historic victory in Bengal. More than 3 lakh central forces have been sent. In UP, they will send 6 lakh. We will exercise the right given under Babasaheb's constitution. We will vote. The public will vote against this government. If you do wrong, the public will stand against you. Akhilesh said- What is the condition of the state's hospitals, treatment is not available anywhere. If you need a bandage on your right hand, they will tie it on your left hand. A living person is being sent to the mortuary. The wrong person is being forcibly taken to the operation theater. Poor people are running away to save their lives. The entire health department has been ruined. 4. 'Irregularities in buying smart meters, harassing the poor' Regarding smart meters, the SP chief said- There have been irregularities in buying smart meters. The government should be asked how much electricity it generated. Solar plants were built, but not thermal plants. Not a single electricity factory was set up. They are harassing people with smart meters. They are harassing the poor. I heard a committee has been formed. This is the Chief Minister's smartness. Whatever happens, form a committee. The Samajwadi government will bring change as soon as it comes. 5. 'BJP has a hidden agenda of votes regarding women's reservation' The SP chief, on Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma's statement about giving Bharat Ratna to CEC Gyanesh Kumar, said that both of them should get the Nobel Prize. Targeting BJP, he said - BJP has a flaw of votes in its mind regarding women's reservation. Now they are talking about veg and non-veg fish. Imagine, veg and non-veg even in fish. BJP says that Sanatani people can eat fish.

stories.title: ₹4 lakh found scattered on Meerut–Shamli highway:Police collect ₹500 and ₹200 notes for 40 minutes; no claimant
stories.summary: An unusual sight was witnessed on the Meerut-Karnal highway in Shamli on Thursday evening. Lakhs of rupees were scattered for about half a kilometer on the highway. When a young man passed by the road covered with notes, he informed the police and also started collecting the bundles. Soon after, the police arrived, and with their help, the notes were collected. When counted, it amounted to approximately 4 lakh rupees. The police have deposited the money in the government treasury. If any claimant comes forward, it will be handed over to them. According to the police, 6 bundles of 500 rupee notes and 5 bundles of 200 rupee notes were found. The incident occurred late on Thursday evening. The young man, Amit Kumar, had collected the notes scattered on the highway and also informed the police. According to Amit, he was going home when money was falling from a biker's bag. He called out to him, but he didn't hear. Bundles of notes found near Baraut Bridge According to the police, on Thursday evening, a call was received on number 112 stating that bundles of notes were scattered on the Meerut-Karnal Highway. A young man named Amit Kumar had given the information. Upon reaching the spot, it was observed that bundles of notes were scattered for about half a kilometer near Baraut Bridge. A young man is collecting the notes. With the help of the young man, a search operation was conducted for about 40 minutes. After this, 6 bundles of 500 rupee notes and 5 bundles of 200 rupee notes were recovered. When the total of 11 bundles was counted, it amounted to approximately 4 lakh rupees. The notes have been deposited in the malkhana (police strongroom/storehouse). So far, no claimant has come forward for it. What did the person who first saw the scattered money say... Amit, who lives near the highway, said- On Thursday evening, between 6-7 PM, he was going from Shamli to his village. A young man passed by on his Splendor bike from a nearby petrol pump. He was going at a high speed. He was carrying a bag. Due to the open chain of the bag, notes were falling out of it. Bundles of notes kept falling for about half a kilometer. Amit said that he called out to the young man many times but he did not hear. Inspector said - Rupees deposited in the Malkhana (store room) Sadar Kotwali in-charge Sujit Sharma said- The recovered amount has been safely deposited in the Malkhana. Efforts are being made to find the real owner of the cash. It is being investigated how such a large amount was scattered on the highway. CCTV footage from nearby areas is being scanned.

stories.title: Pakistani man held in Bulandshahr after 40 years:Fake Aadhaar and driving licence found with suspected sleeper cell agent
stories.summary: A Pakistani man who had been living in Uttar Pradesh for 40 years has been arrested from Bulandshahr. Fake Aadhaar and driving licence were recovered from him. He had been living in several cities of western UP using different names. Police suspect he could be a sleeper cell agent. SP City Abhishek Pratap Ajay said the accused was arrested on Friday evening. His Aadhaar card showed his name as Syed Wasit Ali, son of Syed Laiq Ahmed, resident of 126 Sushila Vihar, Bulandshahr. However, during verification, his passport revealed his real identity as Basid Irshad (55), son of Irshad Ahmed, with an address in New Karachi, Pakistan. The SP added that Basid was earlier arrested in Meerut in 2012 for living illegally by hiding his identity. But questions remain on why he was not deported till now and how he managed to reach Bulandshahr after evading the police. Meerut Police has also been contacted for further details. Information was received from an informant The SP said- We had received information that a young man was living in a rented house for several years by changing his identity. He was planning to commit a crime. After this, checking was started at the police station on Thursday evening. During this, the accused was caught. His mother came to India 45 years ago Basid Irshad’s mother, Bilkis Fatima, came to India in 1981. She had visited relatives living in Sentha village in the Gulawathi area of Bulandshahr. At that time, Basid Irshad was just five years old. He was born in 1976. His mother later remarried in Gulawathi, which helped her get a long-term visa. Basid had also applied for a long-term visa, but his application remained pending. His mother died in 2012, and his stepfather has also passed away. Basid Irshad is married in Meerut and has children. He had been living at different places across Uttar Pradesh. During the investigation, it came out that he is currently working in a private job in Gulawathi. Earlier, he had also worked in Meerut. In 2012, a case was registered against Basid Irshad under the Foreigners Act at Brahmpuri police station in Meerut. Now, a fresh case has been filed against him in Bulandshahr. The police have sent him to judicial custody. He will be taken on remand on Monday after the court reopens. He will remain in jail until the investigation is complete. Later, he will be deported to Pakistan through the Ministry of External Affairs. SP City said - the entire network will be investigated SP City Abhishek Pratap stated that the accused had been living with a fake identity for a long time. The recovered documents were verified by various departments. The role of other people in the case is also being investigated. It is suspected that the youth might also be connected to a sleeper cell of a terrorist organization. This is also being investigated.

stories.title: 1,400-page chargesheet filed against ‘Chhangur Baba’:ED, ATS find ₹100 crore foreign funding, organised Love Jihad racket
stories.summary: A Special ATS court in Lucknow has rejected the discharge plea of self-styled spiritual leader Jalaluddin alias “Chhangur Baba,” clearing the way for trial in a case involving alleged illegal foreign funding and organised religious conversion activities. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) and Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) have filed a detailed chargesheet of nearly 1,400 pages, accusing the main accused and his associates of receiving over ₹100 crore in foreign funds and running a structured network for conversions. Foreign funding trail linked to gulf countries According to investigating agencies, one of the biggest revelations in the case is the flow of foreign funds. The ED has traced transactions exceeding ₹100 crore between 2015 and 2024. The funds were allegedly routed into India from Gulf countries, including Saudi Arabia and Dubai, through multiple accounts and channels to conceal their origin. Authorities claim this money was used to finance conversion activities, offer inducements, and expand the network. The ED also relied on evidence gathered by the ATS, with both agencies coordinating closely to uncover the full extent of the operation. Land purchases used to build network Investigators found that co-accused Naveen and his wife Neetu used the funds to purchase land across multiple districts, including areas in Balrampur. These properties were allegedly used as operational centres for conversion activities. Authorities claim that individuals were lured with financial and social incentives to change their religion. Documents suggest several properties were registered in Neetu’s name, while “Chhangur Baba” is described as playing a key role as a facilitator and alleged patron in the network. Serious charges including conspiracy and sedition The prosecution has invoked multiple serious charges against the accused, including conspiracy against the state, promoting enmity between communities, and fraud. Sections such as 121A (conspiracy against the nation), 153A (promoting religious enmity), and 420 (cheating) of the Indian Penal Code have been applied. If proven, these charges carry stringent penalties. Allegations of conversion through deception The investigation also alleges that non-Muslim women were targeted through fake identities and deceptive relationships. Once trapped, they were allegedly coerced or influenced into religious conversion. Officials claim this was part of an organised and multi-layered operation involving several individuals working at different levels. Court proceedings and key developments After nearly six hours of arguments, Special Judge Neetu Pathak (Court No. 3) rejected the discharge applications of the accused on April 19. The court observed that the allegations were serious and warranted a full trial. The case will now proceed to the next stage, where evidence and witness testimonies will be examined. Additional charges under rape and SC/ST act Further intensifying the case, the prosecution has also added charges of gang rape (Section 376D IPC) involving a Scheduled Caste woman, along with provisions under the SC/ST Act. These additions have made the case more sensitive and serious in the eyes of the court. ATS crackdown uncovered network The Uttar Pradesh ATS initially exposed the network by arresting the main accused from Balrampur. Subsequent raids and investigations led to the identification of other members and their roles. Authorities say the case points to a well-organised and multi-layered network, involving foreign funding, local operations, and coordinated efforts to carry out alleged illegal activities.

stories.title: Man kills wife over fear of affairs in gym:Moradabad businessman says stories about trainers led to insecurity and fatal attack
stories.summary: A scrap trader in Moradabad has been arrested for allegedly murdering his wife, claiming that his growing insecurity over her going to the gym led to the crime. The accused, Shobhit Gupta, was taken into custody on April 23, a day after the incident. During police interrogation, Gupta said he feared his wife might be influenced or misled, citing frequent reports of alleged affairs involving gym trainers. Marriage of 10 years, one daughter Shobhit Gupta, who runs a scrap business in the Double Phatak area of Moradabad, has been married to Poonam Gupta for around 10 years. The couple has a seven-year-old daughter, Aaradhya. Family members said Gupta deeply cared for his wife but often objected to her going to the gym, leading to frequent arguments between them. Read the full story of the murder… Argument turned fatal According to police, on the morning of April 22, after their daughter left for school, Poonam went to the gym as usual. When she returned around 10 am, an argument broke out between the couple over her gym visits. Gupta reportedly asked her to stop going, but she refused. Enraged, he attacked her with an iron handle used for opening shop shutters, striking her multiple times on the head. She collapsed on the floor and died on the spot. Attempt to stage accident After the incident, Gupta allegedly tried to portray the murder as an accident. He placed the body on a bed and waited until evening before informing emergency services. Around 6 pm, he called an ambulance and Dial 112, claiming that his wife had been injured after a fall. However, when police reached the scene and began questioning him, inconsistencies in his statement emerged, leading to his detention and subsequent confession. ‘Stories made me fearful’ During interrogation, Gupta told police that recurring stories about relationships between gym trainers and women had made him increasingly anxious. He admitted that he had no evidence or suspicion of any wrongdoing by his wife but believed gyms were unsafe environments where trainers might try to influence women. He said this fear ultimately led him to take the extreme step, though he claimed he had not intended to kill her. Police action Moradabad SP City Ranvijay Singh confirmed that Gupta has been arrested. The weapon used in the crime—an iron shutter handle—has been recovered. A case has been registered based on a complaint filed by Poonam’s brother. The accused has been produced in court and sent to jail, while further investigation is underway.

stories.title: Dumping ground turns into tourist spot in Gorakhpur:Rapti Eco Park opened for public, offers boating, yoga, kids zone waste-to-wonder attractions
stories.summary: The place in Gorakhpur that was once called a ‘garbage mountain’ has today transformed into a beautiful eco park. The 'Rapti Eco Park' built on approximately 40 acres of land on the Ekla Dam along the Rapti River was inaugurated by the Chief Minister on Thursday and opened to the general public. Prepared at a cost of approximately ₹5 crore, this park has now become a new attractive center for city residents to visit and picnic, where people can spend time with their families, children and friends. Highlights of the park: Waste to Wonder Park: Where attractive figures of peacocks, lions, giraffes and trees and plants have been made from waste. Special Kids Zone for Children: Where swings, seating chairs and decorative items have also been prepared from waste material. Yoga Place in the Middle of the Park: Where people can do yoga amidst nature in the morning and evening; its canopy is made of bamboo, which provides coolness. Pedal Boating for Tourists: Where families and friends can enjoy boating together. Canteen Facility: Canteen arrangement for food and beverages at the entry point. Toilet Facility: Toilet facility for cleanliness. Garden Junction: Different gardens can be seen, beautiful gardens full of greenery, which further enhance the beauty of the park. The most special thing about this park is that many attractions have been created here on the 'Waste to Wonder' theme. Shapes like peacocks, lions, giraffes and trees have been made from garbage and waste materials, which look extremely attractive. A separate kids zone has been created for children, where swings, sitting chairs and even plant pots have been prepared from waste material. Yoga center made from bamboo A beautiful yoga space has also been created in the middle of the park, where people can practice yoga in the open environment during morning and evening. The roof of this yoga space has been specially prepared by artisans from Assam using bamboo, which provides a cooling sensation even in summer. Additionally, pedal boating facilities will also be provided for tourists, so that people can enjoy the riverside. Speaking of facilities, a canteen has been built at the park entrance for food and beverages. Toilet facilities have also been arranged for tourists. A garden full of greenery has been developed throughout the park, which makes it even more beautiful. Earlier it was a mountain of garbage If we talk about the old times, this area was surrounded by large heaps of garbage. This was polluting the Rapti river and the groundwater around it. Along with this, there were frequent problems of fire due to methane gas and foul smell, which also had a bad effect on people's health. The Municipal Corporation worked scientifically to eliminate this problem. Spending about ₹9 crore, 2.26 lakh metric tons of old waste was disposed of through bio-remediation. Through this campaign, approximately 40 acres of land was freed from garbage.

stories.title: Cricketer Abhishek Sharma objects to fans taking selfies in Jaipur:SRH batter says, 'turn off the mobile phone' while visiting Govind Dev Ji temple ahead of IPL match
stories.summary: Before the IPL match in Jaipur, Sunrisers Hyderabad player Abhishek Sharma visited Govind Dev Ji Temple with his mother. Even though he was wearing a white mask, fans recognized him and began taking photos and videos. During this, he stopped one fan and asked them to turn off the camera. A crowd gathered around him inside the temple premises, making him seem slightly uncomfortable. However, at the insistence of some fans, he agreed to take selfies. Earlier, he had sat at the temple entrance with his mother to offer prayers and attend the aarti. Later, he was seen helping his mother through the crowd while leaving. Abhishek Sharma’s team Sunrisers Hyderabad is set to face Rajasthan Royals on April 25 at Sawai Mansingh Stadium. He had arrived in Jaipur with his mother on April 22 for the match. PHOTOS of the cricketer at Govind Dev Ji Temple Abhishek told a fan, ‘Turn off the mobile phone’ Fans became excited after spotting Abhishek Sharma at the temple. Although he was wearing a white mask, fans recognized him. Many then tried to take selfies with him, but security personnel stopped them. Fans began taking selfies and making videos from a distance, after which Abhishek intervened and asked them to stop. Looked uncomfortable in the crowd, fans still took selfies Abhishek Sharma appeared uneasy amid the crowd inside the temple premises. He completed the circumambulation (parikrama) of Govind Dev Ji Temple while surrounded by devotees. Earlier, he and his mother were welcomed by members of the temple committee. Priests conducted the prayer rituals through him, and he was also presented with a symbolic memento of Govind Dev Ji. Abhishek is in Jaipur for the match against Rajasthan Royals Abhishek Sharma is currently in Jaipur for an IPL match. He arrived in Jaipur on April 22 with his mother. Abhishek Sharma is present here with the Sunrisers Hyderabad team. The team's match will be played against Rajasthan Royals at Sawai Mansingh Stadium on April 25. During his Jaipur visit, he took religious darshan and received blessings before the match.

stories.title: Gorakhpur club owner’s son shoots himself, dies:40-year-old reaches farmhouse, makes call before taking his own life
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, Ambarish (40), son of billionaire businessman and Gorakhpur Club operator Atul Srivastava, died by suicide. On Friday, he shot himself in the mouth with his licensed pistol and died on the spot. Ambarish reached his farmhouse alone in his Fortuner at around 8 am on Friday. He was speaking to someone on his mobile when he went upstairs. Between 8:30 am and 9 am, he shot himself. Hearing the gunshot, the farmhouse staff rushed upstairs and found his body lying in a pool of blood. However, the family claims that Ambarish was cleaning his pistol when it accidentally went off. Body found by staff, pistol recovered Farmhouse staff rushed to the spot and found Ambrish lying in a pool of blood. He had sustained a gunshot injury to the face, and a pistol was found in his hand. He was declared dead at the scene. The reason behind the suicide is not yet known. Police and forensic teams investigating Senior Superintendent of Police Dr. Kaustubh reached the spot soon after receiving information. Police have begun questioning staff members, while a forensic team is collecting evidence from the scene. Business background and family details Ambrish lived on Park Road in Gorakhpur and was involved in the tent house business, along with contract work. His company, AK Tent House, was known for providing arrangements at major political and VVIP events. His farmhouse in Kusmhi is located around 10 km from his residence and includes a warehouse on the third floor. Recent public role and family Ambrish was recently elected as the General Secretary of the Shri Chitragupt Temple Sabha. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had attended the oath-taking ceremony of the newly elected office bearers. He is survived by his two young sons, aged 8 and 10. His younger brother Ranu is also a businessman. His father, Atul Srivastava, has previously served as the president of the same temple committee.

stories.title: Yogi Adityanath to inaugurate Rashmirathi festival today:Three-day celebration marks 75 years of Dinkar’s work
stories.summary: A three-day literary and cultural festival, Rashmirathi Parv, will be held in Lucknow from April 24 to 26 to commemorate 75 years of Rashmirathi, the iconic work by national poet Ramdhari Singh Dinkar. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will inaugurate the event on Friday, while Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will attend as the keynote speaker. The festival aims to bring together literature, national discourse, and cultural expression on a single platform. Indira Gandhi Pratishthan to host the event The grand event will take place at Indira Gandhi Pratishthan, where literary figures, scholars, and youth from across the country will participate. The objective is to introduce Dinkar’s literary legacy to the younger generation and strengthen discussions around nationalism and cultural identity. Day 1: National seminar and Theatrical performance The inaugural day (April 24) will begin with the launch of the souvenir Rashmirathi Samvad. This will be followed by a national seminar where scholars will discuss Dinkar’s literary contributions, his ideas on nationalism, and their relevance in contemporary times. In the evening, a stage adaptation based on Rashmirathi will be performed, serving as a major attraction for attendees. Day 2: Focus on Swami Vivekananda’s vision On April 25, discussions will center on the role of Swami Vivekananda in shaping India’s cultural identity. The sessions will aim to inspire youth with messages of self-confidence, national service, and spiritual awareness. A cultural evening will feature a theatrical presentation based on Vivekananda’s life. Day 3: Tribute to Tilak and Atal Bihari Vajpayee The concluding day (April 26) will include discussions on the contributions of Bal Gangadhar Tilak and former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee to nation-building. The event will also feature Atal Swarajali, a musical tribute based on Vajpayee’s poems, along with a theatrical performance on Lokmanya Tilak. Inspiration for youth and cultural pride According to Tourism Minister Jaiveer Singh, the festival is designed to inspire youth with values such as patriotism, self-respect, perseverance, and social harmony. Through Rashmirathi Parv, Uttar Pradesh aims to showcase not only its developmental progress but also its rich cultural heritage.

stories.title: 'If we feel like burden, say it clearly':Ex-MP Brij Bhushan Singh asserts to show relevance of Kshatriya community ahead of 2027 UP polls
stories.summary: Former Kaiserganj MP and BJP leader Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh on Thursday delivered a strong and combative message, saying that if political parties consider him and his community irrelevant, they should state it openly. Singh asserted that the response would be evident in the upcoming state elections. Speaking at the Babu Veer Kunwar Singh Vijay Utsav held at Town Hall in Bhagalpur, Bihar, Singh, without naming any party, accused governments of ignoring certain sections of society and raised concerns about the perceived neglect of the Kshatriya community. “Tell us if we are no longer needed” “Today, in the eyes of governments, we have no existence. If anyone thinks we have become a burden, just say it once—that we are no longer needed. Say it in 2027 or 2029. We will show whether we are relevant or not,” Singh said. He added that the time for persuasion is over and that communities must now recognise and assert their own strength. Call for self-reflection within community Urging introspection, Singh said that the community’s silence in the past had led to its marginalisation. “Whenever we were suppressed, we remained silent. That is why we are not given importance today,” he remarked. He also said that society had failed to secure due recognition for historical figures such as Veer Kunwar Singh, Maharaja Devi Baksh Singh, Rani Lakshmibai, and Birsa Munda. “Credit for freedom limited to a few” Singh alleged that the credit for India’s independence has been confined to a select few, while many revolutionaries have been overlooked. Referring to popular narratives, he remarked that only certain slogans gained prominence, sidelining the ,contributions of others. Quoting a Hindi couplet, he said that those who remain neutral and silent during critical times also bear responsibility, adding that societal silence had proved costly. Questions raised over constitution credit narrative The former MP also questioned the common perception surrounding the framing of the Constitution. He noted that the Constituent Assembly had 242 members, not just Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, and claimed that Bihar had the highest representation at the time. “If anyone disagrees, they are welcome to debate,” he said, calling for a broader recognition of contributions. “Society has lost relevance in government’s eyes” Appealing for introspection, Singh said that if society had followed the ideals of figures like Lord Ram, Bappa Rawal, and Maharana Pratap, it would not be seen as irrelevant today. He reiterated that governments currently do not recognise the community’s significance. Reference to 2023 controversy Referring to past controversies, Singh claimed that he was the target of a “global conspiracy” in 2023 but refused to bow down. Quoting poet Ramdhari Singh Dinkar, he stressed courage and resilience. He also recited lines from the Hanuman Chalisa, stating that a follower of such ideals would not easily submit. “Time to recognise strength, not seek validation” Concluding his address, Singh urged the Kshatriya community to focus on building strength through power, intellect, and knowledge. “This is not the time to keep explaining ourselves, but to recognise our strength,” he said, adding that there is no need for fear or despair.

stories.title: UP temperature soars to 44.4°C amid heatwave:Elephant seen bathing repeatedly; 40 districts face heatwave alert
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh continues to reel under intense heatwave conditions, with scorching temperatures and strong sunlight since Friday morning. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a heatwave alert for 40 districts and a “warm night” alert for 17 districts, indicating little to no relief even during nighttime. Temperature may cross 45°C, rain likely after April 26 According to the IMD, severe heat conditions will persist for the next two days, with temperatures likely to cross 45°C. However, from April 26 onwards, a change in weather is expected, bringing thunderstorms and light rainfall over a four-day period. Meteorologist Atul Singh from Lucknow said that a new weather disturbance will become active from April 26, increasing cloud activity across the state. Initial drizzle is expected in western Uttar Pradesh and Terai regions, followed by thunderstorms and rain statewide. Temperatures may drop by 2–3°C, with fluctuating weather conditions likely until April 29. 4 pictures of the weather Animals struggle as heat intensifies The heatwave is also affecting animals. At Gorakhpur Zoo, an elephant has been seen repeatedly bathing itself to stay cool. In Lucknow Zoo, arrangements such as ice blocks, coolers, and sprinklers have been made for animals. In Kanpur, special provisions like Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) are being given to tigers to help them cope with the heat. Man dies in Kanpur amid heatwave In Kanpur, a 45-year-old man, Sunil Kumar, died while riding pillion on a moving motorcycle. Family members and locals suspect that extreme heat exposure led to his death. Precautionary measures in several districts In view of rising temperatures, authorities in Agra, Mathura, Firozabad, and Mainpuri have banned outdoor labour work between 12 pm and 4 pm to prevent heat-related illnesses. 30 districts cross 40°C, Banda hottest Over the past 24 hours, temperatures in 30 districts of the state have crossed 40°C. Banda recorded the highest temperature at 44.4°C, making it the hottest location in Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: 2 terror suspects linked to Pakistani gangsters arrested:Accused plotted target killings for ₹3 lakh
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) on Thursday arrested two suspected terrorists from Noida, alleging links with Pakistani gangsters and intelligence operatives. Officials said the accused were in contact with handlers across the border and were attempting to build a sleeper cell network in India through social media platforms. According to the ATS, the duo was planning targeted killings using hand grenades, allegedly aiming at specific individuals, with a deal of ₹3 lakh struck for carrying out the attacks. Accused identified, linked to Pakistani operatives During interrogation, one of the accused identified himself as Tushar Chauhan, also known as Hizbullah Ali Khan, a resident of Meerut, while the other, Sameer Khan, is from Delhi. Investigators said both were in contact with Pakistani gangsters Shahzad Bhatti and Abid Jatt. Authorities also claimed that radical Pakistan-based social media influencers were being used to target and influence Indian youth online. Radicalisation and direct contact through social media Tushar reportedly told investigators that he came under the influence of certain individuals and social media content, which gradually drew him toward extremist ideology. During this period, he connected with Shahzad Bhatti and Abid Jatt via Instagram. Their communication later escalated to voice calls, video chats, and push-to-talk platforms. To gain Bhatti’s trust, Tushar allegedly created social media accounts in his name and reconnected even after earlier accounts were blocked. Eventually, he obtained Bhatti’s phone number and began direct communication. Cash incentives and assurances of support Tushar claimed that Bhatti assigned him the task of throwing grenades at specific residences to carry out killings. He was allegedly promised modern weapons and financial incentives—₹50,000 upfront and ₹2.5 lakh after completing the operation. He further stated that he was assured assistance in obtaining a passport and being routed to Pakistan via Dubai. Investigators said references to intelligence agency operatives were also made to reinforce the instructions. A pistol and some cash recovered from him are believed to have been supplied through this network. Co-accused tasked with propaganda activities Sameer Khan was also allegedly in contact with Bhatti through encrypted communication channels. He was assigned the task of writing “TTH” (Tehreek-e-Taliban Hindustan) on public walls and recruiting others into the network. Officials said Sameer and Tushar connected via Instagram and later jointly conducted reconnaissance of potential targets assigned by their handlers. Authorities believe both were prepared to execute the planned attacks. Threats issued, legal action initiated The ATS stated that the accused had issued death threats to several individuals, sometimes during conference calls where Pakistani handlers were also present. Based on digital evidence recovered from their mobile phones and preliminary interrogation, investigators concluded that both were involved in anti-national activities and were preparing to carry out attacks in India under instructions from a Pakistan-based network. A case has been registered at the ATS police station in Lucknow under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Arms Act, and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). Both accused have been produced in court, and further legal proceedings are underway.

stories.title: ₹30 lakh extorted via ‘digital arrest’ scam:Fraud began with fake FedEx call, accused posed as narcotics officials; 2 arrested
stories.summary: Gwalior State Cyber Police have busted a major network involved in fraud under the pretext of “digital arrest” and Telegram trading, arresting two accused. The accused used to impersonate officials from FedEx and the Narcotics Control Bureau to intimidate people and extort lakhs of rupees. Complainant Harshit Dwivedi said the accused called him claiming drugs and illegal items were found in his parcel. The call was then transferred to a supposed narcotics officer. By creating fear of “digital arrest”, they got ₹30,25,719 transferred in the name of “police clearance”. After the complaint, police arrested Saurabh Kumar (24), a resident of Lakhimpur Kheri, and Rajesh Kumar (27). Cyber police traced the accused using fake IP addresses, bank transactions and digital evidence. They were arrested after a raid in Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh. Investigation revealed that the accused opened fake bank accounts to route the fraud money. Transactions worth crores from 16 states were found in these accounts. Around ₹10 lakh from the complainant was directly transferred to the accused’s account. According to police, the accused first posed as courier company employees and then scared victims by claiming drugs were found in parcels. The call was then connected to a fake officer. Through video calls, victims were threatened with “digital arrest” and made to transfer money. Network Spread Across the Country The probe revealed the gang’s network was spread across Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal. The accused kept changing locations to evade arrest. Police-Government Agencies Don't Ask for Money on Video Calls Police clarified that no government agency demands money over phone or video calls and there is no legal provision like “digital arrest”. In such cases, people should immediately report on cyber helpline 1930 and never share OTP or bank details with anyone.

stories.title: BJP dominates UP voter preference on 256 of 403 seats:Samajwadi Party at 135; NDA allies may face maximum losses
stories.summary: Ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh, a large-scale survey conducted by the Dainik Bhaskar app indicates a largely stable political landscape with limited shifts at the top. Across 403 Assembly constituencies, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) emerges as the first preference on 256 seats, while the Samajwadi Party (SP) leads on 135. The most notable losses are projected among BJP’s allies. The Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP), led by Om Prakash Rajbhar, trails on all six of its current seats. Only SP shows gains in the survey A comparison with current seat holdings suggests marginal losses for the BJP and clear gains for the SP. The BJP, which currently holds 258 seats, is projected to fall short by two seats. In contrast, the SP, with 107 seats at present, is estimated to rise to 135 — a net gain of 28 seats. Other parties show either stagnation or decline. Regional trends: gains and losses For analysis, the state was divided into five regions — Purvanchal (133 seats), Awadh (82), Western UP (79), Braj (56), and Bundelkhand (53). The BJP registers gains in Purvanchal and Western Uttar Pradesh, while facing losses in Awadh, Braj, and Bundelkhand. The SP’s performance shows a complementary pattern. It loses ground in Western Uttar Pradesh but expands in Purvanchal, Awadh, Braj, and Bundelkhand. Ministers’ seats: BJP ahead The Council of Ministers comprises 54 members, including the Chief Minister, with 41 MLAs and 13 MLCs. In the survey, the BJP is the first preference on 32 of the 41 ministerial Assembly seats. The SP leads on eight, while BJP ally Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) leads on one. BJP leads on allies’ seats A notable finding is the BJP’s lead on all nine Assembly seats currently held by its allies. On four seats held by Apna Dal (Sonelal) — Bindki, Nanpara, Vishwanathganj, and Shohratgarh — the BJP is the preferred choice. Similarly, on three seats held by the RLD — Khatauli, Thanabhawan, and Siwalkhas — respondents favour the BJP. The trend extends to SBSP-held constituencies, including Mahadeva and Mau, where the BJP also leads. Mau is represented by Abbas Ansari. Opposition gains on NDA seats Of the 290 seats held by the NDA (257 BJP and 33 allies), the SP emerges as the first preference on 75 seats. Within BJP-held constituencies, the SP leads on 59 seats and the Indian National Congress on one. Conversely, the BJP leads on 47 of the SP’s current 105 seats, indicating direct competition between the two principal parties. Muslim-represented constituencies show split trend The Assembly currently has 31 Muslim MLAs — 27 from the SP, two from the RLD, and one each from Apna Dal (S) and SBSP. In these constituencies, the BJP leads on 15 seats, while the SP leads on 16. In several seats represented by Muslim MLAs, including Thanabhawan, Siwalkhas, and Mau, the BJP emerges as the first preference. On the Suar seat, earlier associated with Azam Khan and later won by Apna Dal (S), the SP leads in the survey. First-time MLAs: BJP ahead There are 137 first-time MLAs in the Assembly, including 74 from the BJP and 41 from the SP. The survey places the BJP ahead on 86 of these seats, followed by the SP on 46. Smaller parties register limited preference across the remaining constituencies. Women MLAs: limited change The Assembly has 51 women MLAs — 30 from the BJP, 15 from the SP, four from Apna Dal (S), and one each from the RLD and Congress. The survey indicates minimal change in these constituencies. The BJP leads on 31 seats, the SP on 18, while Apna Dal (S) and Congress lead on one seat each. For each Assembly constituency, the party receiving the highest share of responses was identified as the “first preference”. The findings reflect voter inclination at the time of the survey and not a projection of final results.

stories.title: Samajwadi Party's 300 units free electricity plan under scrutiny:Annual cost could reach ₹82,000 crore, exceeding combined allocations of UP’s top 10 govt depts
stories.summary: Electricity has become a major political flashpoint in Uttar Pradesh. While the government appears on the back foot over the smart meter issue, Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav has announced that his party will provide 300 units of free electricity if it comes to power. If implemented, the scheme—along with existing electricity subsidies—could place an estimated burden of around ₹82,000 crore annually on the state exchequer. This amount exceeds the combined annual budgets of the state’s top 10 departments. Understanding the cost calculations In Uttar Pradesh, electricity consumption between 150 and 300 units is billed at around ₹6.5 per unit. Including meter charges, fixed charges, fuel adjustment charges, and taxes, the effective cost rises to approximately ₹8.5 per unit. According to Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation data, the state currently has around 3.5 crore domestic electricity connections. Of these, nearly 70%—about 2.45 crore consumers—use an average of 300 units per month. Providing 300 units of free electricity to these consumers would cost the state approximately ₹6,240 crore per month, pushing the annual burden to around ₹75,000 crore. The Uttar Pradesh government had presented a budget of about ₹9.13 lakh crore for 2026–27. Of this, ₹6,823 crore was allocated for schemes such as providing 140 units of free electricity to farmers and subsidies for weavers. Combining existing schemes with the proposed free electricity plan for households would take the total expenditure beyond ₹82,000 crore—more than the annual budget of even the power department, which received around ₹66,000 crore this year. Policy concerns: NEP-2026 recommends phasing out free power The trend of free electricity began with the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) during the 2015 Delhi Assembly elections, when it promised 200 units of free power and later implemented it. The scheme continues even after a change in government. Since then, several states have introduced similar schemes. Currently, Karnataka offers 200 units free, Bihar 125 units, and Jharkhand 200 units. Rajasthan provides 150 units free for households with solar panel installations. Additionally, states like Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana, West Bengal, Chhattisgarh, and Jammu Kashmir run subsidy or waiver schemes for farmers, weavers, and low-income households. However, the draft of the National Electricity Policy-2026 (NEP-2026), released by the Power Ministry in January 2026, recommends gradually phasing out free electricity schemes. Samajwadi Party’s stand: Government will bear the cost Former Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary and Samajwadi Party strategist Alok Ranjan stated that free electricity schemes are already operational in several states, including Punjab, which provides 300 units free. He said that in Uttar Pradesh, the burden of such a scheme would not fall on power companies but on the government, which would compensate them through subsidies. With the state budget exceeding ₹9 lakh crore, he argued that the expenditure could be managed. BJP’s response: Wait for the manifesto BJP spokesperson Avneesh Tyagi said the party has already fulfilled its promises of providing electricity and free utilities to farmers. He added that earlier, electricity supply was limited to only a few districts. Regarding the 2027 Assembly elections, he said there is still time, and any concessions would be detailed in the party’s manifesto based on public needs. Why electricity has become a political issue in UP Around 10 to 12 states across India currently offer some form of free electricity or subsidies. With Assembly elections due in Uttar Pradesh in about eight months, electricity has emerged as a key electoral issue. Public anger has been growing over electricity privatization and the rollout of smart prepaid meters. In an election year, even BJP MLAs and councillors have joined public protests. Responding to the backlash, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has formed a committee to investigate technical flaws in smart meters, with a report expected within 10 days. Until then, the replacement of old meters with smart meters has been halted, although new connections continue to receive smart prepaid meters. Amid this backdrop, Akhilesh Yadav’s promise of 300 units of free electricity has further intensified the political battle over power in the state.

stories.title: One school records 14 UP board toppers:5 Intermediate and 9 High School students make merit list
stories.summary: A school in Naubasta, Kanpur, has delivered an exceptional performance in the Uttar Pradesh Board examinations, setting a new record. A total of 14 students from the institution have secured places in the UP Board merit list—five from the Intermediate level and nine from High School. Paritosh Inter College alone contributed all 14 students to the merit list. Among them, Amit Sahu (Intermediate) and Disha Pandey (High School) emerged as city toppers, securing the first position in Kanpur in their respective categories. Focus on discipline and practice drives success School Principal Rachna Awasthi attributed this remarkable achievement to the consistent hard work of both students and teachers. She emphasized that the school maintains a disciplined academic environment throughout the year and encourages regular study habits. Teachers focus not only on subject knowledge but also on answer-writing techniques, guiding students on how to effectively present their responses in exams. Continuous practice sessions are conducted for board students to strengthen their preparation. Additionally, special extra classes are held every Sunday to provide further academic support and guidance. This structured approach has played a key role in delivering such outstanding results this year. Top high school performers from Kanpur All the above students are from Paritosh Inter College, Hanspuram, Naubasta, Kanpur, reflecting the institution’s strong academic foundation and commitment to excellence.

stories.summary: Trinamool Congress alleged that BJP "goons" attacked Arambag MP Mitali Bag's car, vandalizing it and causing her injuries. The party accused Union Home Minister Amit Shah of ordering the attack, calling it an attempt on the MP's life. The incident occurred on the last day of campaigning for the second phase of West Bengal Assembly polls.

stories.title: 'Conspired with BJP to create neutral image': AAP counters Raghav Chadha’s 'toxic work environment' charge
Lokmat Sur Jyotsna Awards pay tribute to classical music; Sumitra Guha, Laxman Pandit honoured
stories.summary: The 13th Sur Jyotsna National Music Awards honored Hindustani vocalists Sumitra Guha and Pandit Laxman Krishnarao Pandit in New Delhi. The ceremony, held at the Dr Ambedkar International Centre, celebrated excellence in Indian classical music and recognized emerging talent. Performances by Kailash Kher and his band marked the event, which also saw the presence of several dignitaries.
